literature.headline_zh: 猴痘病毒（Mpox病毒）本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期猴痘病毒（Mpox病毒）研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 具有完全连接的密集层的 DNN,通过 Adam 优化器的反向传播进行训练,并使用两个和四个隐藏层进行评估。四层网络在损失方面收敛得更快,而跨训练时期的架构之间的准确性没有显着差异。根据提供的测试数据,DNN 的性能优于传统的 ML 模型和其他深度学习方法。 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-11464247/v1]

2024年1月至2026年2月,全球向世卫组织报告确诊病例82,738例,死亡306例(病死率0.37%)。PHEIC 期间占病例数的 74.0%,在 2025 年 5 月达到峰值 7,405 例。模型使用报告病例数和对数人口偏移量;因此,报告的病例率反映的是报告的病例率,而不是真实的感染情况 发病率。报告的 传播 在 2025 年 5 月的峰值后有所下降,但在 PHEIC 终止后仍持续存在。在刚果民主共和国境内,200个卫生区共报告病例144,035例,死亡2,047例(病死率1.42%);这些汇总了疑似/临床兼容和确诊病例。排名前20的卫生区占全国负担的45.4%。 [10.1371/journal.pone.0350572]
在一组真实的临床样本中进行评估时,该检测显示出 100.00% 的特异性、91.67% 的灵敏度和 95.83% 的准确性。数字图像分析将准确度提高到 100%,总分析时间约为 60 分钟。 [10.1016/j.mimet.2026.107761]
治疗 遵守率为 100%。所有 特考韦瑞 治疗的动物均存活至第 28 天完成研究,而两只未治疗的对照动物需要在第 16 天和第 17 天提前安乐死。特考韦瑞 的疗效具有时间依赖性,当第 2 天开始使用 特考韦瑞 时,进行性皮肤病变 AUC 显着降低(P < 0.99)。 [10.1016/j.ebiom.2026.106526]

在 1,449 名参与者中,13.9%(n=202)报告了至少一种健康脆弱行为,主要原因是未接种 猴痘 疫苗(50.4%)、未采取预防保健措施(30.6%)、未接受检测(26.2%)以及不遵循健康 治疗(9.9%)。多变量模型显示,与 猴痘 患者的亲密接触、不披露血清学状态以及不相信与 猴痘 相关的恐同症与较高的 患病率 脆弱行为独立相关,而使用荣耀洞则与较低的 患病率 相关。 [PMCID:PMC13686301]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: A DNN with fully connected dense layers, trained by back-propagation with the Adam optimizer, was evaluated with two and four hidden layers. The four-layer network converged faster in terms of loss, while accuracy did not differ significantly between architectures across training epochs. [10.21203/rs.3.rs-11464247/v1]

Between January 2024 and February 2026, 82,738 confirmed cases and 306 deaths were reported to WHO globally (case fatality ratio 0.37%). The PHEIC period accounted for 74.0% of cases, peaking at 7,405 cases in May 2025. [10.1371/journal.pone.0350572]

The assay demonstrated 100.00% specificity, 91.67% sensitivity, and 95.83% accuracy when evaluated in a panel of real clinical samples. Digital image analysis increased accuracy to 100%, with a total analysis time of approximately 60 minutes. [10.1016/j.mimet.2026.107761]

Treatment adherence was 100%. All tecovirimat-treated animals survived to study completion on Day 28, whereas two untreated control animals required early euthanisation on Days 16 and 17. [10.1016/j.ebiom.2026.106526]

Among the 1,449 participants, 13.9% (n=202) reported at least one health vulnerability behavior, primarily due to not being vaccinated against mpox (50.4%), not adopting preventive care measures (30.6%), not undergoing testing (26.2%), and not following health treatment (9.9%). [PMCID:PMC13686301]

papers.title: Efficacy of Tecovirimat for the Treatment of Mpox Virus Infection in Humans: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
papers.abstract: Tecovirimat has been widely used for the treatment of mpox despite limited evidence supporting its efficacy. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to evaluate the efficacy and safety of tecovirimat for this purpose. PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception to June 5, 2026 for RCTs comparing tecovirimat with placebo or standard care in patients with laboratory-confirmed mpox. Primary outcomes were time to clinical resolution of skin lesions, clinical resolution by day 28-29, and 28-day all-cause mortality. Hazard ratios (HRs) and risk ratios (RRs) were pooled using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman adjustment. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and certainty of evidence using GRADE. Two low-risk-of-bias RCTs involving 941 participants were included. Tecovirimat did not shorten the time to clinical resolution of skin lesions compared with placebo (HR 1.10, 95% CI 0.52-2.31, GRADE: moderate) or increase the lesion resolution by day 28-29 (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.92-1.08, GRADE: high). No statistical heterogeneity was observed (I 2 = 0% for both outcomes). Mortality at day 28 was rare in both trials, precluding meta-analysis. Virological clearance, pain-related outcomes, and serious adverse events were also comparable between treatment groups. In conclusion, current randomized evidence does not support routine tecovirimat use to accelerate clinical recovery or improve mortality rates in patients with mpox, while further evidence is needed to determine whether selected high-risk populations may benefit from antiviral therapy.

papers.title_zh: 特考韦瑞 对人类 猴痘病毒 感染的 治疗 的功效:随机对照试验的系统回顾和荟萃分析。
papers.source_body_en: Tecovirimat has been widely used for the treatment of mpox despite limited evidence supporting its efficacy. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to evaluate the efficacy and safety of tecovirimat for this purpose. PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception to June 5, 2026 for RCTs comparing tecovirimat with placebo or standard care in patients with laboratory-confirmed mpox. Primary outcomes were time to clinical resolution of skin lesions, clinical resolution by day 28-29, and 28-day all-cause mortality. Hazard ratios (HRs) and risk ratios (RRs) were pooled using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman adjustment. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and certainty of evidence using GRADE. Two low-risk-of-bias RCTs involving 941 participants were included. Tecovirimat did not shorten the time to clinical resolution of skin lesions compared with placebo (HR 1.10, 95% CI 0.52-2.31, GRADE: moderate) or increase the lesion resolution by day 28-29 (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.92-1.08, GRADE: high). No statistical heterogeneity was observed (I 2 = 0% for both outcomes). Mortality at day 28 was rare in both trials, precluding meta-analysis. Virological clearance, pain-related outcomes, and serious adverse events were also comparable between treatment groups. In conclusion, current randomized evidence does not support routine tecovirimat use to accelerate clinical recovery or improve mortality rates in patients with mpox, while further evidence is needed to determine whether selected high-risk populations may benefit from antiviral therapy.

papers.title: Global mpox outbreak dynamics during and after the 2024–2026 public health emergency
papers.abstract: The second WHO Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) for mpox was declared on 14 August 2024 after clade Ib monkeypox virus emerged in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and spread rapidly across Africa and internationally. The PHEIC ended on 5 September 2025, and the Africa CDC Public Health Emergency of Continental Security was lifted on 22 January 2026. This study characterised global and Africa-specific mpox epidemiology across the full second PHEIC cycle and immediate post-emergency period, from January 2024 to February 2026. A retrospective surveillance analysis was conducted using the WHO Global Mpox Trends dashboard exported data, supplemented by WHO situation reports S32–S64 and international and national surveillance reports. Analyses included negative binomial segmented regression, travel-linked pathway analysis, exploratory analysis of documented secondary transmission after travel-linked detection, and descriptive statistics. Models used reported case counts with log population offsets; reported case-rate ratios therefore reflect reported case rates rather than true infection incidence. Between January 2024 and February 2026, 82,738 confirmed cases and 306 deaths were reported to WHO globally (case fatality ratio 0.37%). The PHEIC period accounted for 74.0% of cases, peaking at 7,405 cases in May 2025. In total, 163 clade-specific importation or travel-linked detection events were documented across 41 countries within the primary analytic cutoff; documented secondary transmission occurred in 25 (15.3%) events across 16 countries. Within DRC, 200 health zones recorded 144,035 total reported cases and 2,047 deaths (case fatality ratio 1.42%); these aggregate suspected/clinically compatible and confirmed cases. The top 20 health zones accounted for 45.4% of national burden. Reported transmission declined after the May 2025 peak but persisted beyond PHEIC termination. Emergency termination marked an administrative transition, not the end of mpox transmission. The post-emergency period requires sustained surveillance, maintained diagnostic capacity, targeted response in persistent transmission settings, and equitable access to vaccines and countermeasures.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在描述第二次世界卫生组织国际关注的突发公共卫生事件(PHEIC)期间全球和非洲特定的 猴痘 的特征,该事件于 2024 年 8 月 14 日宣布,当时 Ib 分支猴痘病毒在刚果民主共和国(DRC)出现并在非洲和国际范围内迅速传播。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用世卫组织全球 猴痘 趋势仪表板导出的数据进行回顾性 监测 分析,并辅以世卫组织情况报告 S32-S64 以及国际和国家 监测 报告。该研究覆盖 41 个国家,包括 163 个特定分支的输入或与旅行相关的检测事件。
elements_zh.methods: 分析包括负二项式分段回归、旅行相关路径分析、旅行相关检测后记录的次要 传播 的探索性分析以及描述性统计。
elements_zh.main_results: 2024年1月至2026年2月,全球向世卫组织报告确诊病例82,738例,死亡306例(病死率0.37%)。PHEIC 期间占病例数的 74.0%,在 2025 年 5 月达到峰值 7,405 例。模型使用报告病例数和对数人口偏移量;因此,报告的病例率反映的是报告的病例率,而不是真实的感染情况 发病率。报告的 传播 在 2025 年 5 月的峰值后有所下降,但在 PHEIC 终止后仍持续存在。在刚果民主共和国境内,200个卫生区共报告病例144,035例,死亡2,047例(病死率1.42%);这些汇总了疑似/临床兼容和确诊病例。排名前20的卫生区占全国负担的45.4%。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,PHEIC期间占大多数病例,但猴痘在正式终止后仍然持续存在,表明紧急状态的结束标志着行政过渡,而不是猴痘传播的停止。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调需要持续的 监测、保持诊断能力、在持续的 传播 环境中进行有针对性的响应,以及在紧急情况后时期公平获得 疫苗 和对策。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于报告的病例数,这可能无法反映真实的感染情况 发病率,并且病例率比是基于对数人口偏移量。证据是中等的,因为它来自 监测 数据,不包括直接的生物学或临床测量。

papers.title_zh: 2024-2026 年突发公共卫生事件期间和之后的全球 猴痘 暴发 动态
papers.source_body_en: The second WHO Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) for mpox was declared on 14 August 2024 after clade Ib monkeypox virus emerged in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and spread rapidly across Africa and internationally. The PHEIC ended on 5 September 2025, and the Africa CDC Public Health Emergency of Continental Security was lifted on 22 January 2026. This study characterised global and Africa-specific mpox epidemiology across the full second PHEIC cycle and immediate post-emergency period, from January 2024 to February 2026. A retrospective surveillance analysis was conducted using the WHO Global Mpox Trends dashboard exported data, supplemented by WHO situation reports S32–S64 and international and national surveillance reports. Analyses included negative binomial segmented regression, travel-linked pathway analysis, exploratory analysis of documented secondary transmission after travel-linked detection, and descriptive statistics. Models used reported case counts with log population offsets; reported case-rate ratios therefore reflect reported case rates rather than true infection incidence. Between January 2024 and February 2026, 82,738 confirmed cases and 306 deaths were reported to WHO globally (case fatality ratio 0.37%). The PHEIC period accounted for 74.0% of cases, peaking at 7,405 cases in May 2025. In total, 163 clade-specific importation or travel-linked detection events were documented across 41 countries within the primary analytic cutoff; documented secondary transmission occurred in 25 (15.3%) events across 16 countries. Within DRC, 200 health zones recorded 144,035 total reported cases and 2,047 deaths (case fatality ratio 1.42%); these aggregate suspected/clinically compatible and confirmed cases. The top 20 health zones accounted for 45.4% of national burden. Reported transmission declined after the May 2025 peak but persisted beyond PHEIC termination. Emergency termination marked an administrative transition, not the end of mpox transmission. The post-emergency period requires sustained surveillance, maintained diagnostic capacity, targeted response in persistent transmission settings, and equitable access to vaccines and countermeasures.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在描述第二次世界卫生组织国际关注的突发公共卫生事件(PHEIC)期间全球和非洲特定的 猴痘 的特征,该事件于 2024 年 8 月 14 日宣布,当时 Ib 分支猴痘病毒在刚果民主共和国(DRC)出现并在非洲和国际范围内迅速传播。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用世卫组织全球 猴痘 趋势仪表板导出的数据进行回顾性 监测 分析,并辅以世卫组织情况报告 S32-S64 以及国际和国家 监测 报告。该研究覆盖 41 个国家,包括 163 个特定分支的输入或与旅行相关的检测事件。
analysis_zh.methods: 分析包括负二项式分段回归、旅行相关路径分析、旅行相关检测后记录的次要 传播 的探索性分析以及描述性统计。
analysis_zh.main_results: 2024年1月至2026年2月,全球向世卫组织报告确诊病例82,738例,死亡306例(病死率0.37%)。PHEIC 期间占病例数的 74.0%,在 2025 年 5 月达到峰值 7,405 例。模型使用报告病例数和对数人口偏移量;因此,报告的病例率反映的是报告的病例率,而不是真实的感染情况 发病率。报告的 传播 在 2025 年 5 月的峰值后有所下降,但在 PHEIC 终止后仍持续存在。在刚果民主共和国境内,200个卫生区共报告病例144,035例,死亡2,047例(病死率1.42%);这些汇总了疑似/临床兼容和确诊病例。排名前20的卫生区占全国负担的45.4%。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,PHEIC期间占大多数病例,但猴痘在正式终止后仍然持续存在,表明紧急状态的结束标志着行政过渡,而不是猴痘传播的停止。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调需要持续的 监测、保持诊断能力、在持续的 传播 环境中进行有针对性的响应,以及在紧急情况后时期公平获得 疫苗 和对策。

papers.title: Early treatment with tecovirimat against mpox disease in cynomolgus macaques
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Tecovirimat was developed as an antiviral countermeasure against orthopoxviruses and approved by the US Food and Drug Administration Animal Rule based on efficacy in preclinical studies and clinical pharmacokinetic and safety trials. However, recent randomised clinical trials in patients with mpox who initiated tecovirimat an average of 6-9 days after onset of symptoms did not show improvement in time to resolution of skin lesions. Here, we evaluated whether timing of tecovirimat initiation influenced antiviral efficacy following mpox infection in nonhuman primates and defined the therapeutic window for treatment initiation. METHODS: In this randomised preclinical study, 32 cynomolgus macaques were challenged intravenously with 1 × 106 TCID50 mpox clade IIb virus. Oral tecovirimat (10 mg/kg, once daily for 14 days) treatment was initiated on Day 2 (post-exposure and pre-symptomatic), Day 5 (early symptomatic), or Day 9 (peak symptomatic) after mpox challenge, or no treatment was given as a control group. The primary study endpoint was area under the curve (AUC) and peak numbers of progressive skin lesions. The secondary endpoint was AUC and peak levels of plasma viral loads. Additional analyses included total skin lesions, adaptive immune responses, and transcriptomic signatures. FINDINGS: Treatment adherence was 100%. All tecovirimat-treated animals survived to study completion on Day 28, whereas two untreated control animals required early euthanisation on Days 16 and 17. Tecovirimat efficacy was time-dependent. Progressive skin lesion AUC was significantly lower when treatment was initiated on Day 2 (P 0.99). INTERPRETATION: In this randomised preclinical study, tecovirimat demonstrated antiviral therapeutic efficacy but only when initiated early prior to peak viraemia. These findings emphasise the importance of early initiation of treatment and define the therapeutic window for optimal tecovirimat treatment in nonhuman primates. FUNDING: This study was supported by SIGA Technologies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 特考韦瑞 是作为针对 正痘病毒 的 抗病毒药物 对策而开发的,但最近针对 猴痘 患者的临床试验并未显示出皮肤病变消退时间的改善。本研究旨在评估 特考韦瑞 启动时间是否影响非人灵长类动物感染 猴痘 后 抗病毒药物 的疗效。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一项随机临床前研究,涉及 32 只食蟹猴,接受 1 × 106 TCID50 猴痘 clade IIb 病毒静脉注射攻击。该研究为期 28 天,在攻击后第 2 天、第 5 天或第 9 天启动 治疗,或不给予 治疗 作为对照组。
elements_zh.methods: 在攻击后的不同时间点口服 特考韦瑞(10 mg/kg,每天一次,持续 14 天)。主要研究终点是曲线下面积 (AUC) 和进行性皮肤病变的峰值数量,而次要终点是 AUC 和血浆病毒载量的峰值水平。其他分析包括总皮肤损伤、适应性 免疫应答 和转录组特征。
elements_zh.main_results: 治疗 遵守率为 100%。所有 特考韦瑞 治疗的动物均存活至第 28 天完成研究,而两只未治疗的对照动物需要在第 16 天和第 17 天提前安乐死。特考韦瑞 的疗效具有时间依赖性,当第 2 天开始使用 特考韦瑞 时,进行性皮肤病变 AUC 显着降低(P < 0.99)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究表明,特考韦瑞 具有 抗病毒药物 治疗功效,但仅在病毒血症高峰之前尽早开始使用。这些发现定义了非人灵长类动物中最佳 特考韦瑞 治疗 的治疗窗口。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了早期启动 治疗 对 猴痘 的重要性,并为 特考韦瑞 的治疗窗口提供了重要的见解,这可以为 猴痘 患者的未来临床试验和 治疗 方案提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是在非人类灵长类动物中进行的,这可能会限制其对人类的普遍适用性。然而,结果基于随机临床前设计,具有高依从性和完整的随访,支持适度的置信度评估。

papers.title: Deep Learning and Computational Modeling for Epitope-Focused Immunogen Design Targeting Monkeypox
papers.abstract: Abstract Monkeypox (MPX), now widely called mpox, is a zoonotic orthopoxvirus infection that has moved from a neglected tropical disease to a global public health concern. Live-attenuated smallpox vaccines offer cross-protection, but they are produced in limited quantities, are unevenly distributed, and are not suited to every recipient. These constraints motivate the search for rationally designed, epitope-focused immunogens that can be produced at scale and tailored to emerging viral variants. This article describes an in silico framework that combines amino acid feature engineering, classical machine learning (ML) benchmarking, and a deep neural network (DNN) to predict potential T-cell and B-cell epitopes from the MPX virus proteome (VP). Epitope and non-epitope sequences, together with antigen information, were collected from public immunology and virology databases, encoded numerically, and described by a panel of 84 amino acid features. Hierarchical heat-map clustering based on Pearson correlation identified 44 of the 84 features as redundant, and these were removed before modeling. Twenty-eight ML algorithms were then screened; the five best performers, namely Random Forest, Label Spreading, Decision Tree, Label Propagation and Extra Trees, were compared using accuracy, F1 score and the Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), the last two being appropriate for imbalanced data. A DNN with fully connected dense layers, trained by back-propagation with the Adam optimizer, was evaluated with two and four hidden layers. The four-layer network converged faster in terms of loss, while accuracy did not differ significantly between architectures across training epochs. According to the held-out test data, the DNN outperformed the traditional ML models and other deep learning approaches. Because the framework is not specific to one pathogen, it can in principle be retrained to support vaccine design against other emerging infectious diseases. We discuss the biological rationale, methodological choices, limitations, and the experimental validation steps required to move from computational candidates to a multivalent MPX immunogen.

The study highlights the potential of this framework for vaccine design against emerging viral variants, although it is limited to computational analysis without experimental validation. The findings suggest that the framework could be adapted for other pathogens, but its application to mpox requires further biological testing.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 猴痘 (MPX) 现在广泛称为 猴痘,是一种人畜共患的 正痘病毒 感染,已从一种被忽视的热带疾病转变为全球公共卫生问题。这些限制促使人们寻找合理设计、针对表位的免疫原,这些免疫原可以大规模生产并针对新出现的病毒变体进行定制。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项研究描述了一个计算机框架,该框架结合了氨基酸特征工程、经典机器学习 (ML) 基准测试和深度神经网络 (DNN),以预测 MPX 病毒蛋白质组 (VP) 中潜在的 T 细胞和 B 细胞表位。
elements_zh.methods: 表位和非表位序列以及抗原信息是从公共免疫学和病毒学数据库中收集的,进行数字编码,并由一组 84 个氨基酸特征进行描述。基于 Pearson 相关性的分层热图聚类将 84 个特征中的 44 个识别为冗余,并在建模之前将其删除。然后筛选了 28 种 ML 算法;使用准确度、F1 分数和马修斯相关系数 (MCC) 对五个表现最好的方法(即随机森林、标签传播、决策树、标签传播和额外树)进行比较,最后两个适用于不平衡数据。
elements_zh.main_results: 具有完全连接的密集层的 DNN,通过 Adam 优化器的反向传播进行训练,并使用两个和四个隐藏层进行评估。四层网络在损失方面收敛得更快,而跨训练时期的架构之间的准确性没有显着差异。根据提供的测试数据,DNN 的性能优于传统的 ML 模型和其他深度学习方法。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该框架并不特定于一种病原体,因此原则上可以对其进行重新训练,以支持针对其他新出现的传染病的 疫苗 设计。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,所提出的框架可用于设计 猴痘病毒 的多价免疫原,这可以改善 疫苗 的发育和对新兴病毒变体的反应。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于计算机分析,不包括实验验证,这可能会影响结果的普遍性。证据是温和的,因为它基于计算模型并且不涉及直接的生物测试。

papers.title: Severe ocular mpox in an immunocompetent patient
papers.abstract: Mpox, formerly known as monkeypox, is caused by Monkeypox virus (MPXV) and has been associated since 2022 with exanthematous illness in men who have sex with men (MSM), including HIV-negative individuals without prior MPXV vaccination.1,2 The clinical course is usually self-limited, with cutaneous and mucosal involvement.4,10,12 Severe forms, including keratoconjunctivitis and corneal ulcers, are uncommon and have mainly been linked to immunosuppression.2,3,5,10,12,14 We report a 20-year-old MSM male, HIV-negative, immunocompetent, and using pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP). He presented with generalized exanthema, right ocular pain, conjunctival injection, tearing, and periorbital cellulitis.1,2,5,10,14 Ophthalmologic evaluation confirmed severe keratoconjunctivitis with progressive corneal ulcers.5-7,10,11,14 MPXV PCR was positive in skin and corneal samples.1,2,10,14 This case highlights the potential for severe ocular disease in a young, otherwise healthy patient and underscores the need for high clinical suspicion, early ophthalmologic assessment, and timely antiviral therapy.2,4,10,15.

papers.title: Geospatial analysis and predictive modelling of mpox transmission hotspots: a case study of Ogun State, Nigeria
papers.abstract: Mpox is a recurring public health threat in Nigeria and was re-declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern in August 2024. Nigeria's Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response system operates at the Local Government Area (LGA) level, yet published mpox risk models resolve risk only at state level, forcing uniform deployment across heterogeneous LGAs. This study developed and evaluated an LGA-resolution geospatial risk layer for the 20 LGAs of Ogun State and integrated it, as a proof of concept, into a live surveillance platform. State-level records of 40 laboratory-confirmed cases (NCDC, 2022) and 151 suspected cases (Ogun State Ministry of Health, 2022–2024), 191 in total, were spatially disaggregated into 189 pseudo-presence points and modelled with an ensemble of maximum entropy, random forest, and extreme gradient boosting over 100 bootstrap replicates. Discrimination was good under random hold-out (AUC 0.77; Boyce index 0.99) but fell under spatially blocked cross-validation (AUC 0.57), indicating that the layer is suited to coarse triage between tiers rather than within-tier ranking. Seven LGAs were classified high risk along a central corridor anchored on Abeokuta South and the Ijebu–Remo axis, six medium, and seven low. The tiered layer was exported as GeoJSON with tier-specific action packages and integrated into the IDS-Master platform as a proof-of-concept pathway from spatial epidemiology to routine public health surveillance. Because the 189 points were disaggregated from aggregate counts rather than individually geolocated, the tiers should be read as a spatial prior for triage rather than as confirmed case locations.

papers.title: Clade-specific ophthalmic manifestations of mpox: an umbrella review and meta-analysis of systematic reviews.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: On 14 August 2024, the WHO redesignated Monkeypox (mpox) as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. Ocular disease is under-recognised and can cause irreversible vision loss. Clarifying its burden, clade-specific patterns and HIV-related risks is essential for clinical care and public health. METHODS: We conducted an umbrella review and meta-analysis, systematically searching PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library from inception to September 2025. Eligible studies were systematic reviews reporting ophthalmic manifestations in laboratory-confirmed mpox cases, stratified by viral clades I, II and IIb. Pooled proportions were estimated using random-effects meta-analysis, with clade-stratified subgroup analyses. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251137180). RESULTS: Five systematic reviews (36 primary studies; 28 139 patients) were included. The pooled proportion of conjunctivitis was 8.9% (95% CI 4.8 to 13.9), highest in clade I (21.9%) and lowest in clade IIb (2.7%). Keratitis (1.5%), eyelid lesions (3.3%), conjunctival lesions (8.4%) and corneal ulceration (3.3%) varied by clade. Visual impairment occurred in 4.5% overall; unilateral (0.9%) and bilateral (0.4%) blindness were reported only with clade I. Across reviews, people living with advanced HIV experienced disproportionately higher rates of severe and persistent ocular complications than HIV-negative individuals. CONCLUSIONS: Mpox-related ophthalmic disease can cause substantial—and potentially preventable—visual disability. Clade I infection is associated with a greater burden of ocular complications than clade II—particularly IIb. Improved access to eye health services, early recognition and integration of HIV and mpox care are critical to reducing vision loss, especially in resource-limited settings.

The central question is to determine the burden and characteristics of ocular complications caused by mpox, with an emphasis on clade I, II, and IIb.

It systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library from inception to September 2025. Eligible studies were systematic reviews reporting ophthalmic manifestations in laboratory-confirmed mpox cases, stratified by viral clades I, II, and IIb. Pooled proportions were estimated using random-effects meta-analysis, with clade-stratified subgroup analyses. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251137180).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The pooled proportion of conjunctivitis was 8.9% (95% CI 4.8 to 13.9), with the highest rates observed in clade I (21.9%) and the lowest in clade IIb (2.7%). Keratitis (1.5%), eyelid lesions (3.3%), conjunctival lesions (8.4%), and corneal ulceration (3.3%) varied by clade. While clade-specific differences are noted, the evidence is limited by the small number of studies and potential biases in reporting. analysis.summary_en: This umbrella review and meta-analysis of systematic reviews examines the clade-specific ophthalmic manifestations of mpox virus. It identifies significant variations in ocular complications, with clade I showing the highest burden of conjunctivitis and visual impairment, including unilateral and bilateral blindness. The review also highlights the disproportionately higher rates of severe ocular complications in individuals with advanced HIV. These findings underscore the need for improved eye health services and integrated care for mpox and HIV. The review calls for further research and targeted interventions to address these issues, particularly in resource-limited settings.

papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: On 14 August 2024, the WHO redesignated Monkeypox (mpox) as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. Ocular disease is under-recognised and can cause irreversible vision loss. Clarifying its burden, clade-specific patterns and HIV-related risks is essential for clinical care and public health. METHODS: We conducted an umbrella review and meta-analysis, systematically searching PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library from inception to September 2025. Eligible studies were systematic reviews reporting ophthalmic manifestations in laboratory-confirmed mpox cases, stratified by viral clades I, II and IIb. Pooled proportions were estimated using random-effects meta-analysis, with clade-stratified subgroup analyses. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251137180). RESULTS: Five systematic reviews (36 primary studies; 28 139 patients) were included. The pooled proportion of conjunctivitis was 8.9% (95% CI 4.8 to 13.9), highest in clade I (21.9%) and lowest in clade IIb (2.7%). Keratitis (1.5%), eyelid lesions (3.3%), conjunctival lesions (8.4%) and corneal ulceration (3.3%) varied by clade. CONCLUSIONS: Mpox-related ophthalmic disease can cause substantial—and potentially preventable—visual disability. Clade I infection is associated with a greater burden of ocular complications than clade II—particularly IIb. Improved access to eye health services, early recognition and integration of HIV and mpox care are critical to reducing vision loss, especially in resource-limited settings.

Infection Conjunctiva Cornea Eye (Globe) Vision WHAT IS ALREADY KNOWN ON THIS TOPIC Ophthalmic complications of Monkeypox (mpox) have been described, but their overall burden, clade-specific differences and interactions with comorbidities, such as HIV, have not been quantified across reviews. WHAT THIS STUDY ADDS To our knowledge, this is the first umbrella review to provide pooled estimates of mpox-related ocular manifestations across 28 139 patients, showing higher proportions in clade I (Ia/Ib) than clade II (IIa/IIb), and greater severity among people with advanced HIV. HOW THIS STUDY MIGHT AFFECT RESEARCH, PRACTICE OR POLICY Findings support enhanced ophthalmic surveillance in clade I-endemic regions, integration of HIV and mpox services to address syndemic risk and incorporation of eye health into outbreak preparedness, vaccination strategies and clinical care pathways. Introduction Monkeypox (mpox) is a zoonotic disease caused by the mpox virus (MPXV), an Orthopoxvirus closely related to the variola virus, which causes smallpox.1 First identified in monkeys in 1958, MPXV was recognised as a human pathogen in 1970 in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).2 Two distinct clades have been described: clade I (formerly the Congo Basin clade, subdivided into Ia and Ib) and clade II, further divided into IIa and IIb (formerly the West African clade).3 Clade I is more virulent, with an estimated case fatality ratio (CFR) of 10.6%, compared with 1%–3.6% for clade II.4 The 2022 global outbreak was caused by clade IIb, which had a CFR below 0.2%.5 As of August 2025, WHO data indicate substantial global transmission. In Africa alone, more than 43 000 confirmed cases were reported in the previous 12 months, with the DRC (22 222), Uganda (7979) and Sierra Leone (5245) the most affected; up-to-date figures are available via the WHO Global Mpox Dashboard and situation reports.6–8 Although mpox is primarily known for its cutaneous and systemic features—including fever, rash and lymphadenopathy—it can also affect ocular tissues, leading to substantial morbidity and visual impairment.9 Ocular involvement may result from direct viral invasion or immune-mediated mechanisms, ranging from mild conjunctivitis and blepharitis to keratitis, which can cause corneal scarring and vision loss if untreated, in patients with, or who have had, mpox.10 In severe cases, these complications may culminate in permanent visual disability, with major implications for patients affected, health systems and communities.11 Several systematic reviews have summarised evidence on mpox-related ophthalmic complications. However, no study has quantified the global burden or examined clade-specific and region-specific differences in ocular outcomes. To address this gap, we conducted an umbrella review and meta-analysis to synthesise available data on the proportion of ocular manifestations among mpox cases, with a particular focus on clade-specific variation and the influence of healthcare infrastructure. Methods This umbrella review was conducted according to a protocol prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251137180) and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines.12 13 Eligibility criteria Defined using the Population-Outcome-Study design (POS) framework: Population: patients of all ages and demographics diagnosed with mpox. Outcome: ophthalmic manifestations and complications, including but not limited to conjunctivitis, blepharitis, keratitis, corneal lesions, impaired vision and blindness. Study design: systematic reviews and meta-analyses of observational studies, case series and case reports. Only systematic reviews published in English were included. No restrictions were placed on publication date or geography. Where a review used a systematic search but did not fulfil all criteria for a systematic review, this was noted during data extraction. Information sources and search strategy We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library from inception to 11 September 2025. The strategy, developed with an information specialist, combined keywords and Medical Subject Headings related to mpox, ophthalmic manifestations and systematic reviews. The full search strategies are provided in the online supplemental material (annex 1). Supplemental material [bjo-2025-328294supp001.pdf] Study selection Two independent reviewers screened all records in Covidence (Veritas Health Innovation, Melbourne, Australia) in two stages: (1) title/abstract and (2) full text against eligibility criteria. Disagreements were resolved by discussion or adjudication by a third reviewer. Data collection and items A standardised extraction form was piloted. Two reviewers independently extracted study characteristics, mpox clade, ophthalmic manifestations, proportions of ocular outcomes among mpox cases and any reported clade-specific or geographic differences. Discrepancies were resolved by consensus or input from a third reviewer. Data were managed in Microsoft Excel. Clade classification methodology Because many included studies did not specify the MPXV clade, we inferred the clade based on geographic location, study period and epidemiological context: Clade I (Central African clade; Ia and Ib): studies from the DRC, Central African Republic, Republic of the Congo and Sudan. Although Cameroon has historically reported both clades I and II, no Cameroon-specific ocular studies met the inclusion criteria; therefore, Cameroon was not used to assign a clade in pooled analyses. Clade II (West African clade; IIa and IIb): studies from Nigeria and other West African countries primarily correspond to IIa. Subtype IIb was assumed for post2022 studies conducted in non-endemic settings, aligning with the multicountry outbreak beginning in 2022. Risk of bias assessment We appraised the methodological quality of included reviews using AMSTAR 2 (A MeaSurement Tool to Assess Systematic Reviews).14 Two reviewers assessed each study independently; discrepancies were resolved by consensus. Synthesis of results We calculated pooled proportions of ocular manifestations using random-effects meta-analysis (Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation). Subgroup analyses were conducted by clade. Given high heterogeneity (I2>50% in several analyses), we also reported 95% prediction intervals to reflect between-study variability. Terminology ‘Proportion’ refers to the frequency (%) of ocular manifestations among mpox cases in the included studies. Where no timeframe was specified, estimates represent proportion at presentation or during follow-up. Results Characteristics of the included reviews Searches identified 71 records (online supplemental figure 1: PRISMA flow diagram). After removing 23 duplicates, 48 titles/abstracts were screened; 9 full texts were assessed, and 4 were excluded as narrative reviews, leaving 5 eligible systematic reviews (2023–2025; online supplemental table 1). These synthesised 5–25 observational studies each (published 1980–2024). Primary study quality ranged from poor to high, with most studies rated as moderate to high. Risk of bias assessment AMSTAR 2 ratings are reported in online supplemental table 2.14 All five systematic reviews were rated as high quality, indicating generally robust methodology. Sample characteristics of included primary studies 36 studies reporting ocular manifestations in 28 139 patients with mpox were analysed (online supplemental table 3). The studies demonstrated substantial geographic diversity, with data from the USA (n=8), DRC (n=9), Nigeria (n=4), Mexico (n=3), Brazil (n=2), UK (n=2), Spain (n=1), France (n=1), Portugal (n=1), Canada (n=1), Saudi Arabia (n=1), Sudan (n=1), Republic of the Congo (n=1) and multi-country studies (n=2). 23 studies (2022–2024) predominantly represented clade IIb infections from non-endemic regions, while 13 earlier studies documented endemic African outbreaks associated with clade I (n=10) and clade IIa (n=3). No Cameroon-specific ocular studies were identified despite its unique epidemiological position reporting both clades. Several studies highlighted a disproportionate burden of severe and persistent ocular complications among people living with advanced HIV, particularly in clade I settings.15 16 Ophthalmic manifestations by MPXV clade Conjunctivitis by clade Across 25 studies, including 27 022 patients, the pooled proportion of conjunctivitis was 8.86% (95% CI 4.84 to 13.85; prediction interval 0.00% to 43.49%) (figure 1). Clade-specific estimates differed: clade I 21.86% (95% CI 14.74 to 29.87; prediction interval 3.31% to 49.31%; I2=82%), clade IIa 16.91% (95% CI 12.54 to 21.74; prediction interval 9.18%–26.26%) and clade IIb 2.74% (95% CI 0.79 to 5.70; prediction interval 0.00% to 20.86%; I2=97.6%). Wide prediction intervals reflect expected variability across settings and study designs. Keratitis by clade From eight studies (1957 patients), the pooled proportion of keratitis was 1.53% (95% CI 0.75 to 2.55; prediction interval 0.00% to 4.92%) (figure 2). Estimates were higher in clade I at 2.88% (95% CI 1.43 to 4.77; prediction interval 0.00% to 11.29%) than in clade IIa at 0.82% (95% CI 0.31 to 1.51; prediction interval 0.16% to 1.84%). Eyelid lesions by clade Across six studies (816 patients), the pooled proportion of eyelid lesions was 3.25% (95% CI 0.26 to 8.61; prediction interval 0.00% to 27.74%) (figure 3). Clade-specific evidence was limited: clade I 4.26% (95% CI 0.83 to 14.85; single study) and clade IIb 1.11% (95% CI 0.00 to 3.45; single study). An overall pooled estimate labelled ‘clade II’ at 3.94% (95% CI 0.00 to 13.47; prediction interval 0.00% to 52.38%) reflects mixed or unspecified II subtypes; interpret with caution. Conjunctival lesions by clade Across three studies (601 patients), the pooled proportion was 8.37% (95% CI 1.81 to 18.64; prediction interval 0.00% to 64.12%) (figure 4). Clade I was 11.61% (95% CI 2.99 to 24.70; prediction interval 0.00% to 100.00%; I2=93.8%; two studies), while clade II (single study) was 2.13% (95% CI 0.58 to 11.97). Corneal ulceration by clade Across three studies (654 patients), the pooled proportion was 3.33% (95% CI 1.99 to 4.95; prediction interval 0.77–7.23%) (figure 5). Clade I was 3.69% (95% CI 2.32 to 5.35; prediction interval 0.00–18.99%; I2=0%) with consistent rates between studies (3.25% and 4.26%), and clade II (single study) was 2.94% (95% CI 0.85 to 16.19). Visual impairment and blindness by clade Across five studies (986 patients; online supplemental figure 2), the pooled proportion of impaired vision was 4.48% (95% CI 1.30 to 9.21; prediction interval 0.00% to 24.37%). Clade-specific rates varied: clade I 4.20% (95% CI 1.16 to 8.88; prediction interval 0.00% to 32.30%; I2=87.8%), clade II 14.00% (95% CI 6.23 to 26.96; single study) and clade IIb 1.00% (95% CI 0.00 to 5.03; single study). Bilateral blindness (one clade I study; 282 patients; online supplemental figure 4) was 0.35% (95% CI 0.01 to 1.96). papers.title: Monkeypox on a disc: Portable centrifugal microfluidic platform for multi-assay colorimetric LAMP
papers.abstract: Monkeypox is currently the most important orthopoxvirus infection in humans. The increase in the number of cases, combined with its potential social impact and international spread, led the World Health Organization (WHO) to classify it as the most recent Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). Although mainly endemic in resource-limited countries, quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction (qPCR) remains the gold standard for detection but is challenging due to the need for specialized instrumentation. To address this, we propose an instrument-friendly molecular assay based on colorimetric Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP), performed on a multi-assay polystyrene-toner (PST) centrifugal device. The new analytical device was designed to include chambers for loading the LAMP mixture and samples, interconnected channels for mixing them, and separate chambers for simultaneous LAMP amplification and visual detection of each sample. When evaluated in a panel of real clinical samples, compared to qPCR, the assay based on visual detection demonstrated 100.00% specificity, 91.67% sensitivity, and 95.83% accuracy, which increased to 100% accuracy when digital image analysis was employed, with a total analysis time of approximately 60 min. The relative simplicity of the assay may facilitate its implementation in resource-limited settings and contribute to expanding access to molecular detection of monkeypox.

papers.title: SARS, H1N1, EBOLA, COVID-19, MPOX, H5N1 AND HANTAVIRUS: IS HUMANITY ENTERING A NEW ERA OF PANDEMIC? IS TÜRKİYE PREPARED FOR THE NEXT GLOBAL OUTBREAK?
papers.abstract: The emergence and re-emergence of infectious diseases pose persistent challenges to global health security. Outbreaks such as severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), influenza A(H1N1), Ebola virus disease, coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), mpox, avian influenza A(H5N1), and hantavirus infections highlight the need for effective preparedness against emerging infectious threats. The concept of “Disease X” further emphasizes the importance of preparing for unknown pathogens that may cause future epidemics or pandemics. This study aimed to examine major infectious disease outbreaks and assess Türkiye’s preparedness for potential future global outbreaks. A descriptive review design was employed, based on a structured literature search and document analysis of scientific publications and institutional reports. The findings were organized and interpreted using a SWOT framework. The analysis identified healthcare infrastructure, intensive care capacity, digital health systems, and experience gained during the COVID-19 pandemic as potential strengths. However, challenges related to healthcare workforce capacity, zoonotic disease surveillance, public health literacy, coordination across human, animal, and environmental health sectors, and dependence on external sources for certain biotechnological products may constrain preparedness. Climate change, environmental disruption, international travel, migration, and global trade were identified as factors that may influence the emergence and spread of infectious diseases. Strengthening integrated surveillance and early warning systems, improving intersectoral coordination through the One Health approach, enhancing domestic vaccine and diagnostic production capacity, and expanding community-based public health education may help improve Türkiye’s preparedness for future outbreaks. These findings highlight the importance of sustained, multisectoral preparedness for emerging infectious disease threats.
papers.journal: International Journal of Health Services Research and Policy

papers.title_zh: SARS、H1N1、埃博拉、COVID-19、猴痘、H5N1 和汉坦病毒:人类是否正在进入流行病的新时代?土耳其准备好迎接下一个全球 暴发 了吗?
papers.source_body_en: The emergence and re-emergence of infectious diseases pose persistent challenges to global health security. Outbreaks such as severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), influenza A(H1N1), Ebola virus disease, coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), mpox, avian influenza A(H5N1), and hantavirus infections highlight the need for effective preparedness against emerging infectious threats. The concept of “Disease X” further emphasizes the importance of preparing for unknown pathogens that may cause future epidemics or pandemics. This study aimed to examine major infectious disease outbreaks and assess Türkiye’s preparedness for potential future global outbreaks. A descriptive review design was employed, based on a structured literature search and document analysis of scientific publications and institutional reports. The findings were organized and interpreted using a SWOT framework. The analysis identified healthcare infrastructure, intensive care capacity, digital health systems, and experience gained during the COVID-19 pandemic as potential strengths. However, challenges related to healthcare workforce capacity, zoonotic disease surveillance, public health literacy, coordination across human, animal, and environmental health sectors, and dependence on external sources for certain biotechnological products may constrain preparedness. Climate change, environmental disruption, international travel, migration, and global trade were identified as factors that may influence the emergence and spread of infectious diseases. Strengthening integrated surveillance and early warning systems, improving intersectoral coordination through the One Health approach, enhancing domestic vaccine and diagnostic production capacity, and expanding community-based public health education may help improve Türkiye’s preparedness for future outbreaks. These findings highlight the importance of sustained, multisectoral preparedness for emerging infectious disease threats.

papers.title: SPR Analysis of Monkeypox Proteins A29L and E8L Glycan Interaction and Inhibition by Marine-Derived Glycans
papers.abstract: The global resurgence of mpox has established monkeypox virus (MPXV), comprising Clades I and II, as a significant public health threat. Studies of homologous vaccinia virus proteins indicate that cell-surface glycosaminoglycans (GAGs), including heparan sulfate (HS) and chondroitin sulfate (CS), facilitate viral attachment and entry. However, direct interactions between GAGs and MPXV surface proteins A29L/E8L remain poorly characterized. Using surface plasmon resonance (SPR), we quantified the apparent binding affinities of A29L (Clade I KD = 0.8 ± 0.3 nM) and E8L (Clade I KD = 1.2 ± 0.2 nM; Clade II KD = 1.6 ± 0.1 nM) for heparin, a common HS analog. We also quantified E8L apparent binding affinities to CS-A (Clade I KD = 0.4 ± 0.2 nM; Clade II KD = 0.65 ± 0.06 nM) and CS-E (KD = 0.6 ± 0.1 nM; Clade II KD = 0.70 ± 0.08 nM). We further determined that Clade I A29L and E8L preferentially recognized long-chain fully sulfated or N-sulfated heparin. Lastly, we determined a small library of marine-derived sulfated glycans (MSGs) as effective inhibitors for the Clade I E8L and A29L protein-GAG interface. These findings establish previously uncharacterized binding interactions and identify MSGs as potential candidates for anti-mpox drug development.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the interaction between glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) and surface proteins A29L and E8L of monkeypox virus (MPXV) Clades I and II using surface plasmon resonance (SPR). The research highlights the binding affinities of these proteins to heparin and chondroitin sulfate (CS) derivatives, revealing that Clade I proteins preferentially bind to long-chain fully sulfated or N-sulfated heparin. The findings contribute to understanding the specific interactions of MPXV with host GAGs and may inform future strategies for surveillance, diagnosis, and therapeutic interventions.

papers.title_zh: 猴痘蛋白 A29L 和 E8L 聚糖相互作用和海洋衍生聚糖的抑制的 SPR 分析
papers.source_body_en: The global resurgence of mpox has established monkeypox virus (MPXV), comprising Clades I and II, as a significant public health threat. Studies of homologous vaccinia virus proteins indicate that cell-surface glycosaminoglycans (GAGs), including heparan sulfate (HS) and chondroitin sulfate (CS), facilitate viral attachment and entry. However, direct interactions between GAGs and MPXV surface proteins A29L/E8L remain poorly characterized. Using surface plasmon resonance (SPR), we quantified the apparent binding affinities of A29L (Clade I KD = 0.8 ± 0.3 nM) and E8L (Clade I KD = 1.2 ± 0.2 nM; Clade II KD = 1.6 ± 0.1 nM) for heparin, a common HS analog. We also quantified E8L apparent binding affinities to CS-A (Clade I KD = 0.4 ± 0.2 nM; Clade II KD = 0.65 ± 0.06 nM) and CS-E (KD = 0.6 ± 0.1 nM; Clade II KD = 0.70 ± 0.08 nM). We further determined that Clade I A29L and E8L preferentially recognized long-chain fully sulfated or N-sulfated heparin. Lastly, we determined a small library of marine-derived sulfated glycans (MSGs) as effective inhibitors for the Clade I E8L and A29L protein-GAG interface. These findings establish previously uncharacterized binding interactions and identify MSGs as potential candidates for anti-mpox drug development.
papers.abstract_zh: 猴痘 在全球范围内的卷土重来已确定由 I 型和 II 型分支组成的猴痘病毒 (MPXV) 已成为重大的公共卫生威胁。对同源痘苗病毒蛋白的研究表明,细胞表面糖胺聚糖 (GAG),包括硫酸乙酰肝素 (HS) 和硫酸软骨素 (CS),可促进病毒附着和进入。然而,GAG 和 MPXV 表面蛋白 A29L/E8L 之间的直接相互作用仍知之甚少。使用表面等离子共振 (SPR),我们量化了 A29L(Clade I KD = 0.8 ± 0.3 nM)和 E8L(Clade I KD = 1.2 ± 0.2 nM;Clade II KD = 1.6 ± 0.1 nM)对常见 HS 类似物肝素的表观结合亲和力。我们还量化了 E8L 与 CS-A(进化枝 I KD = 0.4 ± 0.2 nM;进化枝 II KD = 0.65 ± 0.06 nM)和 CS-E(KD = 0.6 ± 0.1 nM;进化枝 II KD = 0.70 ± 0.08 nM)的表观结合亲和力。我们进一步确定,Clade I A29L 和 E8L 优先识别长链完全硫酸化或 N-硫酸化肝素。最后,我们确定了一个小型海洋源性硫酸聚糖 (MSG) 文库作为 Clade I E8L 和 A29L 蛋白-GAG 界面的有效抑制剂。这些发现建立了以前未表征的结合相互作用,并将 MSG 确定为抗 猴痘 药物开发的潜在候选者。

papers.title: Single-Step Sample-Activated Alternating Sequential Flow Enables Autonomous Multistep Electrochemical Lateral Flow Detection of Mpox Virus DNA
papers.abstract: Abstract The 2022 multinational mpox virus (MPXV) outbreak and continued cross-border transmission have highlighted limitations of laboratory-confined PCR diagnostics. Here, we report an alternating lateral flow architecture (ALFA) that transforms traditional single-pass lateral flow into a programmable platform for autonomous multistep electrochemical nucleic acid detection following a single prepared-sample introduction. By regulating passive fluid delivery, ALFA enables sequential molecular processing and in situ signal generation without external intervention. Coupled with Ag(I)-mediated mismatch DNA nanocomplexes (MDNs), the system provides electrochemical signal amplification without nucleic acid amplification. ALFA detected MPXV DNA with a limit of detection (LOD) of 1.55 pM and a linear range of 101−105 pM. In urine and saliva spiked with structurally intact viral particles, the lowest statistically distinguishable concentration was 10 copies mL−1. Clinical evaluation of 50 PCR-characterized lesion swab samples yielded 92.11% sensitivity, 100% specificity, and 94.0% accuracy. The platform also maintained stable performance over an estimated 112 days. ALFA therefore provides a programmable lateral flow framework for rapid, amplification-free, decentralized nucleic acid diagnostics.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the limitations of traditional PCR diagnostics during the 2022 multinational mpox virus (MPXV) outbreak and ongoing cross-border transmission.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the clinical evaluation of 50 PCR-characterized lesion swab samples to assess the performance of the ALFA platform.
analysis.methods: The ALFA platform was developed using an alternating lateral flow architecture, with passive fluid delivery enabling sequential molecular processing and in situ signal generation. It was coupled with Ag(I)-mediated mismatch DNA nanocomplexes (MDNs) for electrochemical signal amplification without nucleic acid amplification.
analysis.main_results: The ALFA system detected MPXV DNA with a limit of detection (LOD) of 1.55 pM and a linear range of 101−105 pM. In urine and saliva spiked with structurally intact viral particles, the lowest statistically distinguishable concentration was 10 copies mL−1.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as demonstrating the potential of ALFA to provide rapid, amplification-free, decentralized nucleic acid diagnostics for mpox virus detection, which is a novel approach compared to traditional PCR methods.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that ALFA could enhance surveillance and diagnosis of mpox virus in decentralized settings, improving public health responses to outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's clinical evaluation was based on a limited number of samples, and the performance was assessed in a controlled environment, which may limit generalizability. The evidence strength is moderate due to these constraints.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces an innovative ALFA platform for mpox virus detection, which enables autonomous multistep electrochemical nucleic acid detection without the need for nucleic acid amplification. The system demonstrated a limit of detection of 1.55 pM and a linear range of 101−105 pM, with the ability to detect as low as 10 copies mL−1 in urine and saliva samples. The platform's performance was validated using 50 PCR-characterized lesion swab samples, yielding 92.11% sensitivity, 100% specificity, and 94.0% accuracy. The authors interpret these results as a novel approach to decentralized diagnostics, which could improve surveillance and response to mpox outbreaks. However, the study's limited sample size and controlled environment suggest a moderate level of evidence strength.

papers.title_zh: 单步样品激活交替顺序流可实现 猴痘病毒 DNA 的自主多步电化学侧流检测
papers.source_body_en: Abstract The 2022 multinational mpox virus (MPXV) outbreak and continued cross-border transmission have highlighted limitations of laboratory-confined PCR diagnostics. Here, we report an alternating lateral flow architecture (ALFA) that transforms traditional single-pass lateral flow into a programmable platform for autonomous multistep electrochemical nucleic acid detection following a single prepared-sample introduction. By regulating passive fluid delivery, ALFA enables sequential molecular processing and in situ signal generation without external intervention. Coupled with Ag(I)-mediated mismatch DNA nanocomplexes (MDNs), the system provides electrochemical signal amplification without nucleic acid amplification. ALFA detected MPXV DNA with a limit of detection (LOD) of 1.55 pM and a linear range of 101−105 pM. In urine and saliva spiked with structurally intact viral particles, the lowest statistically distinguishable concentration was 10 copies mL−1. Clinical evaluation of 50 PCR-characterized lesion swab samples yielded 92.11% sensitivity, 100% specificity, and 94.0% accuracy. The platform also maintained stable performance over an estimated 112 days. ALFA therefore provides a programmable lateral flow framework for rapid, amplification-free, decentralized nucleic acid diagnostics.

papers.title: Identification of Mpox Skin Lesion Images Based on Deep Learning Classification Models
papers.abstract: Mpox (formerly known as monkeypox) is a rare zoonotic disease that can cause skin lesions and has the potential for global spread. With the deepening integration of computer science and medicine, intelligent disease detection models based on deep learning and neural networks have become important auxiliary tools for enhancing clinical diagnosis and treatment. This study conducted a comparative analysis of the performance of mainstream deep learning classification models,VGG19, ResNet50, DenseNet201, GoogLeNet, and ConvNeXt_B,in the task of mpox skin image recognition. For the binary classification task, images were categorized into a “Mpox” class and an “Others” class, where the latter includes chickenpox and measles cases, given that their initial rash and pustule presentations closely resemble those of mpox. Beyond quantitative performance evaluation, this study further employed GradCAM++ to generate class activation heatmaps, providing visual interpretability of model decision-making. The resulting heatmaps offer critical clinical diagnostic value by highlighting key lesion regions, thereby enhancing model transparency and supporting clinicians in validating predictions. The experimental results indicate that under identical model parameters and learning rates, the ResNet50 model achieved higher classification accuracy and inference speed, demonstrating its application potential for accurate diagnosis in mpox and other disease image recognition tasks.
papers.journal: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence

papers.title_zh: 基于深度学习分类模型的猴痘皮肤病变图像识别
papers.source_body_en: Mpox (formerly known as monkeypox) is a rare zoonotic disease that can cause skin lesions and has the potential for global spread. With the deepening integration of computer science and medicine, intelligent disease detection models based on deep learning and neural networks have become important auxiliary tools for enhancing clinical diagnosis and treatment. This study conducted a comparative analysis of the performance of mainstream deep learning classification models,VGG19, ResNet50, DenseNet201, GoogLeNet, and ConvNeXt_B,in the task of mpox skin image recognition. For the binary classification task, images were categorized into a “Mpox” class and an “Others” class, where the latter includes chickenpox and measles cases, given that their initial rash and pustule presentations closely resemble those of mpox. Beyond quantitative performance evaluation, this study further employed GradCAM++ to generate class activation heatmaps, providing visual interpretability of model decision-making. The resulting heatmaps offer critical clinical diagnostic value by highlighting key lesion regions, thereby enhancing model transparency and supporting clinicians in validating predictions. The experimental results indicate that under identical model parameters and learning rates, the ResNet50 model achieved higher classification accuracy and inference speed, demonstrating its application potential for accurate diagnosis in mpox and other disease image recognition tasks.

papers.title: HECA-YOLOv11: A High-Accuracy Hybrid Attention Network for Real-Time Monkeypox Skin Lesion Detection with Interpretability
papers.abstract: Introduction: The global outbreak risk of monkeypox necessitates efficient diagnostic tools. Current methods are slow and struggle to differentiate similar skin lesions, while deep learning models lack both accuracy and interpretability for multi-class classification. This study aims to develop a high-performance, real-time screening tool for early detection of monkeypox and similar conditions. Methods: This study proposes an enhanced architecture that incorporates the Highly Efficient Channel Attention (HECA) mechanism into YOLOv11 to improve feature selection. HECA performs Global Average Pooling (GAP) and Max Average Pooling (MAP) on input feature maps. Using spatial transformations and pixel-domain enhancements, the research establishes and augments a four-class dataset containing monkeypox, measles, chickenpox, and normal skin images. Gradient-Weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) generates heatmaps for lesion localization visualization, while a PyQt5-based interactive diagnostic interface streamlines clinical workflows. Results: Experimental results demonstrate the proposed model’s superior performance compared to existing approaches (EfficientNet-v2-l, GoogLeNet, ResNet50, VGG19, MobileNetv2, DenseNet201, and YOLOv11s) on the test set, with enhanced detection speed, accuracy (98.9%), precision (99%), recall (99.3%), and F1-score (99.1%). HECA-YOLOv11 outperforms SE-YOLOv11 and ECA-YOLOv11 by over 5.1% across all evaluation metrics. Heatmap analysis confirms the model’s focus on lesion regions, aligning with medical reasoning. Discussion: The integrated attention mechanism and interpretability techniques effectively address key limitations in automated skin lesion detection. The high performance and low latency signify a major advancement towards reliable clinical decision support, with important implications for early outbreak containment. Conclusion: The HECA-YOLOv11 framework provides a highly accurate and efficient tool for early monkeypox screening. Its standardized interface holds significant potential to accelerate public health responses and improve global control of emerging infectious diseases.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the urgent public-health need for rapid, accurate diagnostic tools to mitigate the global outbreak risk of mpox, highlighting that existing methods are slow and deep learning models lack both accuracy and interpretability for multi-class skin lesion classification.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The authors developed and evaluated a deep learning framework (HECA-YOLOv11) designed for real-time screening of mpox and similar skin lesions using a four-class image dataset.
analysis.methods: The proposed architecture integrates a Highly Efficient Channel Attention (HECA) mechanism into YOLOv11, applying Global Average Pooling and Max Average Pooling to input feature maps, and augments a dataset containing monkeypox, measles, chickenpox, and normal skin images using spatial transformations and pixel-domain enhancements.
analysis.main_results: On the test set, HECA-YOLOv11 achieved 98.9% accuracy, 99% precision, 99.3% recall, and 99.1% F1-score, outperforming EfficientNet-v2-l, GoogLeNet, ResNet50, VGG19, MobileNetv2, DenseNet201, YOLOv11s, SE-YOLOv11, and ECA-YOLOv11 by over 5.1% across all metrics.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the integrated attention mechanism and interpretability techniques as effectively addressing key limitations in automated skin lesion detection, marking a major advancement toward reliable clinical decision support for early mpox screening.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The standardized interface and high performance of HECA-YOLOv11 suggest potential to accelerate public health responses and improve global control of emerging infectious diseases through early detection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report dataset size, geographic or demographic scope, external validation, or prospective clinical evaluation, limiting generalisability and leaving the strength of evidence moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces HECA-YOLOv11, a deep learning framework that integrates a Highly Efficient Channel Attention mechanism into YOLOv11 to improve real-time detection of mpox skin lesions. Using a four-class dataset augmented with spatial and pixel-domain enhancements, the model achieved 98.9% accuracy, 99% precision, 99.3% recall, and 99.1% F1-score on the test set, outperforming multiple baselines by over 5.1% across all metrics. Heatmap analysis via Grad-CAM confirmed lesion-focused attention, and a PyQt5 interface was developed to streamline clinical workflows. The authors argue this represents a major advancement toward reliable clinical decision support for early mpox screening and could accelerate public health responses. However, the abstract-only evidence lacks dataset size, external validation, and prospective clinical evaluation, constraining generalisability and evidence strength.

papers.title_zh: HECA-YOLOv11:一种高精度混合注意力网络,用于实时猴痘皮肤病变检测并具有可解释性
papers.source_body_en: Introduction: The global outbreak risk of monkeypox necessitates efficient diagnostic tools. Current methods are slow and struggle to differentiate similar skin lesions, while deep learning models lack both accuracy and interpretability for multi-class classification. This study aims to develop a high-performance, real-time screening tool for early detection of monkeypox and similar conditions. Methods: This study proposes an enhanced architecture that incorporates the Highly Efficient Channel Attention (HECA) mechanism into YOLOv11 to improve feature selection. HECA performs Global Average Pooling (GAP) and Max Average Pooling (MAP) on input feature maps. Using spatial transformations and pixel-domain enhancements, the research establishes and augments a four-class dataset containing monkeypox, measles, chickenpox, and normal skin images. Gradient-Weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) generates heatmaps for lesion localization visualization, while a PyQt5-based interactive diagnostic interface streamlines clinical workflows. Results: Experimental results demonstrate the proposed model’s superior performance compared to existing approaches (EfficientNet-v2-l, GoogLeNet, ResNet50, VGG19, MobileNetv2, DenseNet201, and YOLOv11s) on the test set, with enhanced detection speed, accuracy (98.9%), precision (99%), recall (99.3%), and F1-score (99.1%). HECA-YOLOv11 outperforms SE-YOLOv11 and ECA-YOLOv11 by over 5.1% across all evaluation metrics. Heatmap analysis confirms the model’s focus on lesion regions, aligning with medical reasoning. Discussion: The integrated attention mechanism and interpretability techniques effectively address key limitations in automated skin lesion detection. The high performance and low latency signify a major advancement towards reliable clinical decision support, with important implications for early outbreak containment. Conclusion: The HECA-YOLOv11 framework provides a highly accurate and efficient tool for early monkeypox screening. Its standardized interface holds significant potential to accelerate public health responses and improve global control of emerging infectious diseases.
papers.abstract_zh: 简介:全球 暴发 猴痘风险需要高效的诊断工具。目前的方法速度缓慢,并且难以区分相似的皮肤病变,而深度学习模型缺乏多类分类的准确性和可解释性。本研究旨在开发一种高性能、实时筛查工具,用于早期检测猴痘和类似病症。方法:本研究提出了一种增强的架构,将高效通道注意力(HECA)机制纳入 YOLOv11 中,以改进特征选择。HECA 对输入特征图执行全局平均池化 (GAP) 和最大平均池化 (MAP)。该研究利用空间变换和像素域增强,建立并增强了包含猴痘、麻疹、水痘和正常皮肤图像的四类数据集。梯度加权类激活映射 (Grad-CAM) 生成用于病变定位可视化的热图,而基于 PyQt5 的交互式诊断界面则简化了临床工作流程。结果:实验结果表明,与测试集上的现有方法(EfficientNet-v2-l、GoogLeNet、ResNet50、VGG19、MobileNetv2、DenseNet201 和 YOLOv11s)相比,所提出的模型具有优越的性能,具有增强的检测速度、准确度(98.9%)、精确度(99%)、召回率(99.3%)和 F1 分数(99.1%)。在所有评估指标中,HECA-YOLOv11 的性能均优于 SE-YOLOv11 和 ECA-YOLOv11 超过 5.1%。热图分析证实了该模型对病变区域的关注,与医学推理相一致。讨论:集成的注意力机制和可解释性技术有效地解决了自动皮肤病变检测的关键限制。高性能和低延迟标志着可靠临床决策支持的重大进步,对早期 暴发 遏制具有重要意义。结论:HECA-YOLOv11框架为早期猴痘筛查提供了高度准确和高效的工具。其标准化界面在加速公共卫生应对和改善新发传染病的全球控制方面具有巨大潜力。

papers.title: Healthcare Workers’ Preparedness for Monkeypox Pandemic Response in SubSaharan Africa: A Rapid Review Investigating the Knowledge Gap
papers.abstract: Background: Mpox is a zoonotic viral disease caused by an Orthopoxvirus endemic to sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), where its resurgence underscores the urgent need for improved preparedness among health care workers (HCWs). Despite the potential of a One Health approach, current implementations remain fragmented. This rapid review synthesises evidence on HCWs' knowledge, attitudes, information sources, and barriers to preparedness regarding Mpox in SSA to identify training needs and policy implications. Methods: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, PubMed and ScienceDirect were searched using MeSH terms and Boolean operators for studies published between 2000 and 2024. Studies assessing HCW knowledge, attitudes, or preparedness for Mpox in SSA with full-text availability in English or French were included; those involving non-HCW populations, conducted outside SSA, or lacking primary data were excluded. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data using a standardised template; quality was assessed using the JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical CrossSectional Studies. Results: Five studies from 388 records were included (Cameroon, Ethiopia, Nigeria, DRC; n = 1,672 HCWs). Only 46.8% of HCWs demonstrated adequate Mpox knowledge. Barriers included reliance on social media and limited access to formal training. Positive attitudes towards prevention correlated with higher knowledge levels. Conclusion: Fewer than half of SSA HCWs demonstrate adequate Mpox knowledge despite a regional case fatality rate nearly ten times the global average; positive attitudes are not translating into clinical preparedness, reflecting a critical intention-action gap; and social media dominates as an information source, underscoring the need for peer-reviewed alternatives within a One Health training framework.

analysis.summary_en: This rapid review examines healthcare workers' (HCWs) preparedness for monkeypox (Mpox) pandemic response in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). The review highlights that only 46.8% of HCWs have adequate knowledge about Mpox, despite its high case fatality rate in the region. Barriers to preparedness include reliance on social media for information and limited access to formal training. Positive attitudes towards prevention are associated with higher knowledge levels, but these attitudes do not translate into clinical preparedness, indicating an intention-action gap. The review underscores the need for peer-reviewed information sources and a structured One Health training framework to address these gaps. The findings suggest that targeted training and policy interventions are essential to improve HCW readiness for Mpox outbreaks in SSA.

Results: Five studies from 388 records were included (Cameroon, Ethiopia, Nigeria, DRC; n = 1,672 HCWs). Only 46.8% of HCWs demonstrated adequate Mpox knowledge. Barriers included reliance on social media and limited access to formal training. Positive attitudes towards prevention correlated with higher knowledge levels. Conclusion: Fewer than half of SSA HCWs demonstrate adequate Mpox knowledge despite a regional case fatality rate nearly ten times the global average; positive attitudes are not translating into clinical preparedness, reflecting a critical intention-action gap; and social media dominates as an information source, underscoring the need for peer-reviewed alternatives within a One Health training framework.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:猴痘 是一种人畜共患病毒性疾病,由撒哈拉以南非洲 (SSA) 流行的 正痘病毒 引起,该病的死灰复燃凸显了改善卫生保健工作者 (HCW) 准备情况的迫切需要。尽管“同一个健康”方法具有潜力,但目前的实施仍然分散。本快速审查综合了 HCW 的知识、态度、信息来源以及 SSA 中 猴痘 准备障碍的证据,以确定培训需求和政策影响。方法:按照系统评价和荟萃分析的首选报告项目 (PRISMA) 指南,使用 MeSH 术语和布尔运算符对 2000 年至 2024 年间发表的研究进行 PubMed 和 ScienceDirect 搜索。纳入了评估 HCW 知识、态度或 SSA 中 猴痘 准备情况的研究,并提供英文或法文全文;那些涉及非医护人员人群、在 SSA 之外进行或缺乏主要数据的研究被排除在外。两名评审员使用标准化模板独立筛选和提取数据;使用 JBI 分析横断面研究批判性评估清单评估质量。结果:纳入了来自 388 份记录的五项研究(喀麦隆、埃塞俄比亚、尼日利亚、刚果民主共和国;n = 1,672 名医护人员)。只有 46.8% 的医护人员表现出足够的 猴痘 知识。障碍包括对社交媒体的依赖和获得正规培训的机会有限。对预防的积极态度与较高的知识水平相关。结论:尽管该地区的病死率接近全球平均水平的十倍,但只有不到一半的 SSA 医护人员表现出足够的 猴痘 知识;积极态度并未转化为临床准备,反映了严重的意向与行动差距;社交媒体作为信息来源占据主导地位,强调了在同一个健康培训框架内需要经过同行评审的替代方案。
