papers.full_text: AbstractObjective To analyze adherence to health vulnerability behaviors among men who have sex with men during the mpox public health emergency in Brazil. Method A cross-sectional, analytical study conducted in a virtual environment between September and December 2022 via an electronic questionnaire, with recruitment via social media/dating apps. The outcome of interest comprised four variables related to health vulnerability behaviors, and a multivariable analysis was conducted using a generalized linear model. Results A total of 1,449 men who reported having sex with men participated in the study, with a prevalence of health vulnerability behaviors of 13.9% (n=202), mainly due to not being vaccinated against mpox (50.4%), not adopting preventive care measures (30.6%), not undergoing testing (26.2%), and not following health treatment (9.9%). The multivariable model indicated a higher prevalence of the outcome independently associated with intimate contact with a person with mpox (adjusted prevalence ratio [APR]: 1.82; 95% confidence interval [95%CI] 1.33; 2.48), non-disclosure of serological status (APR 1.40; 95%CI 1.05; 1.87), and disbelief in mpox-related homophobia (APR 1.39; 95%CI 1.01; 1.90). The use of glory holes was associated with a lower prevalence (APR 0.43; 95%CI 0.20; 0.92). Conclusion Greater health vulnerability was identified among participants who exhibited behaviors associated with a higher risk of mpox exposure, highlighting the need to plan targeted, population-based actions.Keywords: Sexual Vulnerability; Risk-Taking; Men’s Health; Mpox, Monkeypox; Cross-Sectional Studies ResumoObjetivo Analisar a adesão a comportamentos de vulnerabilidade à saúde entre homens que fazem sexo com homens na emergência de saúde pública de mpox no Brasil. Método Estudo transversal, analítico, realizado em ambiente virtual entre setembro e dezembro de 2022 via questionário eletrônico, com recrutamento em redes sociais/aplicativos de relacionamento. O desfecho de interesse do estudo foi composto por quatro variáveis de comportamentos de vulnerabilidade à saúde e foi aplicada regressão multivariada dos dados pelo modelo de regressão linear generalizado. Resultados Participaram do estudo 1.449 homens que afirmaram fazer sexo com homens, uma prevalência de comportamentos de vulnerabilidade à saúde de 13,9% (n=202), principalmente por não se vacinarem contra a mpox (50,4%), não adotarem medidas de cuidado (30,6%), não realizarem testagem (26,2%) e não seguirem tratamento de saúde (9,9%). O modelo multivariado indicou maior prevalência do desfecho associada independentemente a contato íntimo com pessoa com mpox (razões de prevalência ajustada [RP ajustada]: 1,82; intervalos de confiança de 95% [IC95%] 1,33; 2,48), a não revelação do status sorológico (RP ajustada 1,40; IC95% 1,05; 1,87) e à descrença em homofobia relacionada à mpox (RP ajustada 1,39; IC95% 1,01; 1,90). O uso de glory holes (buracos da glória) associou-se à menor prevalência (RP ajustada 0,43; IC95% 0,20; 0,92). Conclusão Identificou-se maior vulnerabilidade à saúde entre participantes que apresentaram comportamentos relacionados ao maior risco de exposição ao mpox, o que enseja planejamento de ações populacionais específicas.Palavras-chave: Vulnerabilidade Sexual, Assunção de Riscos, Saúde do Homem, Mpox, Estudos Transversais MethodsStudy designThis is a cross-sectional, analytical, and quantitative study conducted via a web survey, that is, an electronic questionnaire applied exclusively in a virtual environment. This manuscript followed the recommendations of the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE).SettingData collection took place between September and December 2022, a period that coincided with the mpox outbreak in Brazil, during which reported cases were more concentrated in the states of São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro [15]. Participants were recruited exclusively in a virtual environment, through digital social networks (Facebook, Instagram, X), instant messaging applications (WhatsApp and Telegram), and dating and sexual networking applications (Hornet, Grindr, Scruff, and Tinder), all with a recognized queer and/or gay perspective. To enable participation, a specific research profile was created on these platforms, including a study description with a link to access the electronic questionnaire.ParticipantsThe study population consisted of Brazilian men who used social networks and interaction applications. Inclusion criteria were: self-identifying as a man (cisgender or transgender); having had at least one sexual encounter with another man in the past 12 months; being 18 years of age or older; and residing in Brazil. Individuals who were outside the country during the data collection period were excluded from the analysis. Identification and recruitment of participants were conducted online through the dissemination of the research profile on social networks, instant messaging applications, and dating applications.Data sources and measurementData collection was carried out via an electronic questionnaire hosted on the REDCap platform. The instrument, validated (face and content) by five experts and five participants, consisted of 46 questions distributed across four sections: (a) sociodemographic information; (b) sexual-affective relationships; (c) sexual behaviors and practices; (d) use of health services, experiences, proximity, and perceptions regarding stigma/fear related to mpox.Recruitment combined two strategies. First, the virtual snowball sampling technique [16] was used, in which 20 men who have sex with men, selected as “seeds” (diverse in terms of region, race/skin color, income, and education), were invited to share the research link within their networks. Second, direct dissemination was carried out through profiles created for the study on social networks (Facebook, Instagram, X), messaging applications (WhatsApp, Telegram), and dating applications (Hornet, Grindr, Scruff, and Tinder).VariablesThe study outcome was a dichotomous variable (yes/no) composed of four behaviors: (1) would follow mpox treatment if diagnosed; (2) would undergo mpox testing if a testing center were available; (3) would receive vaccination against mpox, if the vaccine was available; (4) would take measures for self-care and notify contacts if diagnosed. If a participant responded “no” to at least one of the aforementioned variables, they were classified as “adherent to at least one health vulnerability behavior,” defined as at least one negative response regarding testing, treatment, vaccination, or contact notification related to mpox.These behaviors were presented in the results of this manuscript, all measured dichotomously (yes/no): “Presented at least one vulnerability behavior”; “Presented two or more vulnerability behaviors”; “Would not be vaccinated against mpox”; “Would not take self-care/contact notification measures”; “Would not undergo mpox testing”; and “Would not follow treatment if diagnosed”. The first two variables were used exclusively for sample description.Independent variables comprised three main dimensions:Sociodemographic: being a young adult (<30 years) (yes/no); gender identity (cis/trans); homosexual orientation (yes/no); marital status (without a partner/with a partner); race/skin color (White/Non-White, including Black, Brown [Brazilian mixed race], Asian, and Indigenous, grouped according to recommendations [17]); having a religion (yes/no); higher education (yes/no); formal income (yes/no).Psychosocial variables: previous diagnosis of mpox (yes/no); knowing people close who were diagnosed with mpox (yes/no); intimate contact with a person diagnosed with mpox (yes/no); would disclose mpox serological status (yes/no); fear of being discriminated against by health services (yes/no); fear of being discriminated against by friends (yes/no); fear of being discriminated against by family (yes/no); belief that someone may face homophobia because of mpox (yes/no).Behavioral variables: type of sexual partnership (last six months) (no partner/fixed/fixed+casual); was immunized against COVID-19 (yes/no); stopped engaging in casual sex after the mpox outbreak (yes/no); would undergo pre- and post-exposure testing for mpox (yes/no); condomless sexual practice (yes/no); uses apps to seek sex (yes/no); uses saunas to seek sex (yes/no); seeks sex in public places (parties and clubs) (yes/no); use of glory hole (yes/no); practice of chemsex (yes/no); practice of cruising (yes/no); practice of bugchasing (yes/no); challenging sexual practices (yes/no); and participation in orgies (yes/no).The following practices were defined based on previous studies [16,18]: (a) double penetration: simultaneous sexual penetration by two or more penises; (b) challenging sexual practice: consistent engagement in two or three of these practices, defined based on the circumstances in which they occur; (c) fisting or footing: anal penetration using the fist or foot; (d) cruising: free, consensual, and anonymous sex practiced between men in public spaces, such as parks, wooded areas, beaches, or parking lots; (e) glory hole: a round opening in a wall that allows insertion of the penis, so that someone on the other side can use it sexually in various ways; (f) bugchasing: when an HIV-negative man deliberately seeks an HIV-positive man to become infected. To define chemsex, participants were asked whether they had used illicit drugs immediately before and/or during sexual intercourse in the past 12 months. For those who answered yes, a multiple-choice list was presented to indicate the specific drugs used [18].BiasTo reduce selection bias, the virtual snowball technique was adopted, favoring the inclusion of participants from different regions, sociodemographic profiles, and sexual contexts. The questionnaire underwent face and content validation and pilot testing, which minimized measurement bias. Online data collection allowed for greater anonymity, reducing underreporting of stigmatized practices.Study sizeSample size calculation was performed using G*Power software, version 3.1.9.7, considering the population of men aged >18 years in Brazil. The assumed prevalence was 50% (to maximize sample size due to the lack of prior data on this phenomenon), with a tolerable standard error of 3% and a 95% confidence level. The estimated sample size at the end was 1,067 men.Statistical methodsStatistical analyses were conducted using IBM SPSS software (SPSS Inc., Chicago, IL, USA), version 27.0. An exploratory analysis was performed to describe the distribution of predictor variables in relation to health vulnerability behavior, with data presented as absolute and relative frequencies.Pearson’s chi-square test was used to assess the association between predictor variables and adherence to health vulnerability behaviors and to screen candidate variables for the initial multivariable model. Variables with p-value<0.020 in the bivariate analysis were considered eligible to compose this model.The presence of multicollinearity was investigated using tolerance coefficients and the variance inflation factor (VIF). The final stage of the analysis consisted of multivariable modeling to identify factors independently associated with health vulnerability behavior among men who have sex with men. The generalized linear Poisson regression model was applied with a log link function because the outcome prevalence was >10%. Adherence to the Poisson distribution was assessed using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test (p-value>0.005) and the assumption of equidispersion. The calculation of adjusted prevalence ratios (APR) and 95% confidence intervals (95%CI) used the hybrid parameter estimation method, the robust variance estimator, and Type III analysis to test model effects. The omnibus test was used to evaluate the hypothesis of the final multivariable model, which explains factors associated with health vulnerability behavior, against a model containing only the intercept, at a significance level of 5% (p-value<0.005). The final model was adjusted for age and showed a good fit to the data (deviance 771.862; AIC 1.187.862; BIC 1.219.517; log-likelihood –587.931). The omnibus test indicated that the overall model was significant (χ2(5)=23.048; p-value<0.001). The significance of the APR for variables included in the final model was assessed using the Wald chi-square test, with variables having p-values<0.005 considered significant. Study designThis is a cross-sectional, analytical, and quantitative study conducted via a web survey, that is, an electronic questionnaire applied exclusively in a virtual environment. This manuscript followed the recommendations of the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE). Statistical methodsStatistical analyses were conducted using IBM SPSS software (SPSS Inc., Chicago, IL, USA), version 27.0. An exploratory analysis was performed to describe the distribution of predictor variables in relation to health vulnerability behavior, with data presented as absolute and relative frequencies.Pearson’s chi-square test was used to assess the association between predictor variables and adherence to health vulnerability behaviors and to screen candidate variables for the initial multivariable model. Variables with p-value<0.020 in the bivariate analysis were considered eligible to compose this model.The presence of multicollinearity was investigated using tolerance coefficients and the variance inflation factor (VIF). The final stage of the analysis consisted of multivariable modeling to identify factors independently associated with health vulnerability behavior among men who have sex with men. The generalized linear Poisson regression model was applied with a log link function because the outcome prevalence was >10%. Adherence to the Poisson distribution was assessed using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test (p-value>0.005) and the assumption of equidispersion. The calculation of adjusted prevalence ratios (APR) and 95% confidence intervals (95%CI) used the hybrid parameter estimation method, the robust variance estimator, and Type III analysis to test model effects. The omnibus test was used to evaluate the hypothesis of the final multivariable model, which explains factors associated with health vulnerability behavior, against a model containing only the intercept, at a significance level of 5% (p-value<0.005). The final model was adjusted for age and showed a good fit to the data (deviance 771.862; AIC 1.187.862; BIC 1.219.517; log-likelihood –587.931). The omnibus test indicated that the overall model was significant (χ2(5)=23.048; p-value<0.001). The significance of the APR for variables included in the final model was assessed using the Wald chi-square test, with variables having p-values<0.005 considered significant. ResultsAmong study participants, 13.9% (n=202) of the 1,449 men who reported having sex with men presented at least one health vulnerability behavior, while 86.1% (n=1,247) reported none of these behaviors. Among vulnerable participants, 17.3% (n=35/202) presented two or more vulnerability behaviors. Specifically, 50.4% (n=102/202) reported that they would not be vaccinated against mpox, 30.6% (n=62/202) stated that they would not take self-care/contact notification measures, 26.2% (n=53/202) that they would not undergo mpox testing, and 9.9% (n=20/202) reported that they would not follow treatment if diagnosed (Table 1).Table 1Distribution of health vulnerability behaviors among men who have sex with men in the context of mpox. Brazil, 2022 (n=1,449)VariablesYes n (%)No n (%)Vulnerable n=202 (%)Presented at least one vulnerability behavior202 (13.9)1,247 (86.1)-Presented two or more vulnerability behaviors35 (2.4)1,414 (97.6)17.3 (35)Would not be vaccinated against mpox102 (7.0)1,347 (93.0)102 (50.4)Would not take self-care/contact notification measures62 (4.3)1,387 (95.7)62 (30.6)Would not undergo mpox testing53 (3.7)1,396 (96.3)53 (26.2)Would not follow treatment if diagnosed20 (1.4)1,429 (98.6)20 (9.9)Of the total study participants, young adults (<30 years) were identified (n=654; 45.1%), who were predominantly cisgender (n=1,400; 96.6%) and reported a homosexual orientation (n=1,222; 84.3%). Marital status without a partner was more frequent (n=1,094; 75.5%), as well as non-White race/skin color (n=867; 59.8%). Regarding religiosity, 49.5% (n=717) reported being religious. full_text_sections.abstract: AbstractObjective To analyze adherence to health vulnerability behaviors among men who have sex with men during the mpox public health emergency in Brazil. Method A cross-sectional, analytical study conducted in a virtual environment between September and December 2022 via an electronic questionnaire, with recruitment via social media/dating apps. The outcome of interest comprised four variables related to health vulnerability behaviors, and a multivariable analysis was conducted using a generalized linear model. Results A total of 1,449 men who reported having sex with men participated in the study, with a prevalence of health vulnerability behaviors of 13.9% (n=202), mainly due to not being vaccinated against mpox (50.4%), not adopting preventive care measures (30.6%), not undergoing testing (26.2%), and not following health treatment (9.9%). The multivariable model indicated a higher prevalence of the outcome independently associated with intimate contact with a person with mpox (adjusted prevalence ratio [APR]: 1.82; 95% confidence interval [95%CI] 1.33; 2.48), non-disclosure of serological status (APR 1.40; 95%CI 1.05; 1.87), and disbelief in mpox-related homophobia (APR 1.39; 95%CI 1.01; 1.90). The use of glory holes was associated with a lower prevalence (APR 0.43; 95%CI 0.20; 0.92). Conclusion Greater health vulnerability was identified among participants who exhibited behaviors associated with a higher risk of mpox exposure, highlighting the need to plan targeted, population-based actions.Keywords: Sexual Vulnerability; Risk-Taking; Men’s Health; Mpox, Monkeypox; Cross-Sectional Studies ResumoObjetivo Analisar a adesão a comportamentos de vulnerabilidade à saúde entre homens que fazem sexo com homens na emergência de saúde pública de mpox no Brasil. Método Estudo transversal, analítico, realizado em ambiente virtual entre setembro e dezembro de 2022 via questionário eletrônico, com recrutamento em redes sociais/aplicativos de relacionamento. O desfecho de interesse do estudo foi composto por quatro variáveis de comportamentos de vulnerabilidade à saúde e foi aplicada regressão multivariada dos dados pelo modelo de regressão linear generalizado. Resultados Participaram do estudo 1.449 homens que afirmaram fazer sexo com homens, uma prevalência de comportamentos de vulnerabilidade à saúde de 13,9% (n=202), principalmente por não se vacinarem contra a mpox (50,4%), não adotarem medidas de cuidado (30,6%), não realizarem testagem (26,2%) e não seguirem tratamento de saúde (9,9%). O modelo multivariado indicou maior prevalência do desfecho associada independentemente a contato íntimo com pessoa com mpox (razões de prevalência ajustada [RP ajustada]: 1,82; intervalos de confiança de 95% [IC95%] 1,33; 2,48), a não revelação do status sorológico (RP ajustada 1,40; IC95% 1,05; 1,87) e à descrença em homofobia relacionada à mpox (RP ajustada 1,39; IC95% 1,01; 1,90). O uso de glory holes (buracos da glória) associou-se à menor prevalência (RP ajustada 0,43; IC95% 0,20; 0,92). Conclusão Identificou-se maior vulnerabilidade à saúde entre participantes que apresentaram comportamentos relacionados ao maior risco de exposição ao mpox, o que enseja planejamento de ações populacionais específicas.Palavras-chave: Vulnerabilidade Sexual, Assunção de Riscos, Saúde do Homem, Mpox, Estudos Transversais
full_text_sections.methods: MethodsStudy designThis is a cross-sectional, analytical, and quantitative study conducted via a web survey, that is, an electronic questionnaire applied exclusively in a virtual environment. This manuscript followed the recommendations of the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE).SettingData collection took place between September and December 2022, a period that coincided with the mpox outbreak in Brazil, during which reported cases were more concentrated in the states of São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro [15]. Participants were recruited exclusively in a virtual environment, through digital social networks (Facebook, Instagram, X), instant messaging applications (WhatsApp and Telegram), and dating and sexual networking applications (Hornet, Grindr, Scruff, and Tinder), all with a recognized queer and/or gay perspective. To enable participation, a specific research profile was created on these platforms, including a study description with a link to access the electronic questionnaire.ParticipantsThe study population consisted of Brazilian men who used social networks and interaction applications. Inclusion criteria were: self-identifying as a man (cisgender or transgender); having had at least one sexual encounter with another man in the past 12 months; being 18 years of age or older; and residing in Brazil. Individuals who were outside the country during the data collection period were excluded from the analysis. Identification and recruitment of participants were conducted online through the dissemination of the research profile on social networks, instant messaging applications, and dating applications.Data sources and measurementData collection was carried out via an electronic questionnaire hosted on the REDCap platform. The instrument, validated (face and content) by five experts and five participants, consisted of 46 questions distributed across four sections: (a) sociodemographic information; (b) sexual-affective relationships; (c) sexual behaviors and practices; (d) use of health services, experiences, proximity, and perceptions regarding stigma/fear related to mpox.Recruitment combined two strategies. First, the virtual snowball sampling technique [16] was used, in which 20 men who have sex with men, selected as “seeds” (diverse in terms of region, race/skin color, income, and education), were invited to share the research link within their networks. Second, direct dissemination was carried out through profiles created for the study on social networks (Facebook, Instagram, X), messaging applications (WhatsApp, Telegram), and dating applications (Hornet, Grindr, Scruff, and Tinder).VariablesThe study outcome was a dichotomous variable (yes/no) composed of four behaviors: (1) would follow mpox treatment if diagnosed; (2) would undergo mpox testing if a testing center were available; (3) would receive vaccination against mpox, if the vaccine was available; (4) would take measures for self-care and notify contacts if diagnosed. If a participant responded “no” to at least one of the aforementioned variables, they were classified as “adherent to at least one health vulnerability behavior,” defined as at least one negative response regarding testing, treatment, vaccination, or contact notification related to mpox.These behaviors were presented in the results of this manuscript, all measured dichotomously (yes/no): “Presented at least one vulnerability behavior”; “Presented two or more vulnerability behaviors”; “Would not be vaccinated against mpox”; “Would not take self-care/contact notification measures”; “Would not undergo mpox testing”; and “Would not follow treatment if diagnosed”. The first two variables were used exclusively for sample description.Independent variables comprised three main dimensions:Sociodemographic: being a young adult (<30 years) (yes/no); gender identity (cis/trans); homosexual orientation (yes/no); marital status (without a partner/with a partner); race/skin color (White/Non-White, including Black, Brown [Brazilian mixed race], Asian, and Indigenous, grouped according to recommendations [17]); having a religion (yes/no); higher education (yes/no); formal income (yes/no).Psychosocial variables: previous diagnosis of mpox (yes/no); knowing people close who were diagnosed with mpox (yes/no); intimate contact with a person diagnosed with mpox (yes/no); would disclose mpox serological status (yes/no); fear of being discriminated against by health services (yes/no); fear of being discriminated against by friends (yes/no); fear of being discriminated against by family (yes/no); belief that someone may face homophobia because of mpox (yes/no).Behavioral variables: type of sexual partnership (last six months) (no partner/fixed/fixed+casual); was immunized against COVID-19 (yes/no); stopped engaging in casual sex after the mpox outbreak (yes/no); would undergo pre- and post-exposure testing for mpox (yes/no); condomless sexual practice (yes/no); uses apps to seek sex (yes/no); uses saunas to seek sex (yes/no); seeks sex in public places (parties and clubs) (yes/no); use of glory hole (yes/no); practice of chemsex (yes/no); practice of cruising (yes/no); practice of bugchasing (yes/no); challenging sexual practices (yes/no); and participation in orgies (yes/no).The following practices were defined based on previous studies [16,18]: (a) double penetration: simultaneous sexual penetration by two or more penises; (b) challenging sexual practice: consistent engagement in two or three of these practices, defined based on the circumstances in which they occur; (c) fisting or footing: anal penetration using the fist or foot; (d) cruising: free, consensual, and anonymous sex practiced between men in public spaces, such as parks, wooded areas, beaches, or parking lots; (e) glory hole: a round opening in a wall that allows insertion of the penis, so that someone on the other side can use it sexually in various ways; (f) bugchasing: when an HIV-negative man deliberately seeks an HIV-positive man to become infected. To define chemsex, participants were asked whether they had used illicit drugs immediately before and/or during sexual intercourse in the past 12 months. For those who answered yes, a multiple-choice list was presented to indicate the specific drugs used [18].BiasTo reduce selection bias, the virtual snowball technique was adopted, favoring the inclusion of participants from different regions, sociodemographic profiles, and sexual contexts. The questionnaire underwent face and content validation and pilot testing, which minimized measurement bias. Online data collection allowed for greater anonymity, reducing underreporting of stigmatized practices.Study sizeSample size calculation was performed using G*Power software, version 3.1.9.7, considering the population of men aged >18 years in Brazil. The assumed prevalence was 50% (to maximize sample size due to the lack of prior data on this phenomenon), with a tolerable standard error of 3% and a 95% confidence level. The estimated sample size at the end was 1,067 men.Statistical methodsStatistical analyses were conducted using IBM SPSS software (SPSS Inc., Chicago, IL, USA), version 27.0. An exploratory analysis was performed to describe the distribution of predictor variables in relation to health vulnerability behavior, with data presented as absolute and relative frequencies.Pearson’s chi-square test was used to assess the association between predictor variables and adherence to health vulnerability behaviors and to screen candidate variables for the initial multivariable model. Variables with p-value<0.020 in the bivariate analysis were considered eligible to compose this model.The presence of multicollinearity was investigated using tolerance coefficients and the variance inflation factor (VIF). full_text_sections.discussion: DiscussionThis study identified that social and behavioral factors strongly influenced the adoption of health vulnerability behaviors among men who have sex with men during the mpox outbreak in Brazil. Having intimate contact with individuals diagnosed with mpox, not disclosing serological status, and not recognizing the possibility of homophobia-related discrimination were associated with higher vulnerability, whereas the use of alternative sexual practices, such as glory holes, emerged as a protective factor. These findings showed that risk perception and the ways individuals negotiate intimacy directly impact preventive health behaviors.The study had some limitations. The sample included users of social networks/dating applications recruited via virtual snowball sampling, which may have limited participation of individuals with lower digital access and introduced selection bias. Data collection was self-reported and anonymous, which, although it ensures confidentiality and encourages participation, may introduce recall and social desirability biases. The cross-sectional design may prevent causal inference. The categorization of race/skin color into “White” and “Non-White,” due to the low number of Black and Indigenous individuals in the sample, may have limited intersectional analysis. This limitation highlights the importance of future studies that are racially representative and employ broader analytical approaches. The creation of a composite outcome was also a limitation, as it combined distinct behaviors with different underlying causes. Nevertheless, the study provided relevant evidence for understanding how social inequalities and perceptions of stigma shape health vulnerability.In the multivariable model, intimate contact with a person diagnosed with mpox was the most strongly associated factor. Emotional closeness may reduce risk perception and lead to less cautious decision-making [19]. The possibility of denial or risk minimization among individuals exposed to the virus should be considered, indicating the need for post-exposure testing and contact monitoring strategies [20]. In situations where the virus is already present in an immediate social circle (e.g., a diagnosed individual), risk perception may be underestimated, leading to less cautious behavior [9] and a false sense of familiarity and trust among intimate partners, resulting in lower adherence to preventive measures [21]. In contexts of emotional/sexual closeness, there is a tendency to overlook basic precautions, highlighting the need for educational strategies focused on individuals close to diagnosed persons [21,22].Non-disclosure of mpox serological status was relevant, as it was associated with a higher likelihood of health vulnerability behaviors, possibly linked to fear of discrimination/stigma and homophobia [23,24]. This silence, although socially protective, increases individual and collective vulnerability and disrupts transmission chains [25]. Anti-stigma actions to enable disclosure of serological status without social retaliation should be implemented [26]. The disbelief in the possibility of homophobia associated with mpox was associated with a higher likelihood of health vulnerability behaviors. This finding suggests that minimizing the impact of prejudice may lead to a lower perception of social risk and, consequently, to reduced preventive care [26]. The denial of discrimination risk indicates a distancing from the reality of experiencing prejudice, highlighting the need for educational campaigns that integrate both biological and social risk dimensions. It reinforces that perceived social risk (discrimination) influences health behaviors among men who have sex with men, underscoring the need for broader awareness campaigns that go beyond biological framing and include the social consequences of the disease and empathy [26,27]. On the other hand, using glory holes for sexual activity appeared protective. This may reflect a perceived reduction in direct contact, even though the practice still carries significant risks of transmitting infection. This finding highlights the complexity of self-protection strategies, which may simultaneously be perceived as protective and risky [28]. The use of glory holes may involve sexual activities with exposure to bodily fluids, representing a considerable risk for the spread of infections such as mpox [28]. There was a predominance of behaviors such as condomless sex (bareback), use of apps to find partners, and the presence of casual and steady partners. These behaviors can be identified as risk factors for the transmission of sexually transmitted infections, as shown in previous studies in Brazil [29]. However, some participants reported behavioral changes, such as stopping casual sexual encounters after the mpox outbreak, indicating opportunities for educational interventions [20,29].In the context of mpox, health vulnerability among men who have sex with men is shaped by social and behavioral factors, ranging from intimate contact with diagnosed individuals to non-disclosure of serological status and underestimation of homophobia, as well as the rejection of alternative sexual strategies that may function as relative protection. Addressing this vulnerability, beyond individual-level behaviors among affected populations, requires integrating biomedical measures with stigma reduction, safe care environments, equitable public policies, qualified listening practices, and social justice.
full_text_sections.other: Ethical aspectsThis research respected ethical principles, having obtained the following approval data: Research ethics committee Universidade Federal da BahiaOpinion number 6,065,498Approval date 30/8/2022Certificate of submission for ethical appraisal 61180222.8.0000.5531Informed consent form Obtained from all participants prior to data collection. IntroductionThe monkeypox virus, belonging to the genus Orthopoxvirus [1], gained notoriety following reports of human cases in endemic regions of West and Central Africa, particularly in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, where it remains endemic with sporadic outbreaks documented [2]. In May 2022, a confirmed case in the United Kingdom was followed by cases in several other previously non-endemic countries, demonstrating the virus’s rapid global spread [2].Transmission to humans occurs through contact with bodily fluids from infected animals or humans [3]. In this context, mpox infection has gained epidemiological relevance due to global mobility, increased international travel, migratory flows, and interconnectivity among countries, all of which favor its spread [2].Between January and December 2022, the World Health Organization (WHO) reported approximately 83,000 cases in 110 countries, of which 98% were among men with a mean age of 36 years. Of these, 95% were men who have sex with men, particularly in the 18 to 44-year age group, highlighting the vulnerability of this population [4]. Considering this scenario, WHO classified the 2022 outbreak as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC), exposing weaknesses in containment strategies, equitable access, and the provision of health care, as well as the impact of social stigma and barriers faced by vulnerable groups [4,5].The characterization of the outbreak among men who have sex with men was marked by efforts in public health awareness actions and media communication, which ultimately reinforced prejudice and discrimination [5]. The response to mpox in this population, as in the HIV/AIDS pandemic, prompted reflections on society and health systems regarding epidemiological crises affecting historically marginalized groups [5]. In Brazil, between 2022 and July 2025, 14,458 mpox cases and 17 deaths were confirmed, with a peak in 2022 (10,840 cases), a sharp decline in 2023 (847 cases), a resurgence in 2024 (2,065), and a new decline in 2025 (706 by the end of that year). The burden is concentrated in the Southeast, particularly in the states of São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro, the latter leading, and, in 2025, the highest incidences occurred in Santa Catarina, Amazonas, and the Federal District. The profile of cases remains predominantly male and composed of young adults (mean age of 33 years). Among records with available information, sexual relations with men predominate, although there is a relevant proportion of missing data in variables related to sexual orientation and behavior [6].Health vulnerability behaviors are attitudes, habits, or conditions that increase the risk of health problems and hinder the adoption of preventive practices and access to appropriate care. Such behaviors affect individuals’ health outcomes and, when linked to the social determinants of health, imply discrimination and stigma, highlighting the multifactorial nature of health-risk practices [7].Stigma and discrimination may hinder access to health services, compromising the search for testing and early treatment [8]. Previous studies have suggested that the marginalization of men who have sex with men modifies the sexual behavior of this population, leading to an increase in unprotected sexual practices, multiple sexual partners, among other behaviors, which contributed to the spread of mpox during the 2022 outbreak [9,10]. The gap in educational and preventive campaigns, in turn, increases the risk of epidemic outbreaks in contexts of resource scarcity and low vaccination coverage, and delays decision-making by health authorities in providing care to vulnerable populations [11].In 2024, Brazil implemented a vaccination coverage plan for populations at risk of mpox transmission as one of the measures to contain the disease [12]. However, adherence was hindered by unequal vaccine distribution, vaccine hesitancy, and limited information about vaccine safety [12]. In the same year, the resurgence of cases with the identification of clade Ib, a more infectious and potentially more severe variant than the 2022 mpox virus lineages, in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and neighboring countries, reinforced the need for more effective prevention and response strategies and the expansion of vaccination coverage [12,13]. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to analyze adherence to health vulnerability behaviors among men who have sex with men during the mpox public health emergency in Brazil, addressing the need to understand risk factors for health vulnerability in this population.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional, analytical study was conducted in a virtual environment between September and December 2022, involving 1,449 men who reported having sex with men. The study focused on health vulnerability behaviors in the context of mpox in Brazil.
analysis.methods: The study used an electronic questionnaire hosted on the REDCap platform, with data collected via social media and dating apps. A generalized linear Poisson regression model with a log link function was applied to analyze the prevalence of health vulnerability behaviors, considering the outcome prevalence of >10%.
analysis.main_results: Among the 1,449 participants, 13.9% (n=202) reported at least one health vulnerability behavior, primarily due to not being vaccinated against mpox (50.4%), not adopting preventive care measures (30.6%), not undergoing testing (26.2%), and not following health treatment (9.9%). The multivariable model showed that intimate contact with a person with mpox, non-disclosure of serological status, and disbelief in mpox-related homophobia were independently associated with higher prevalence of vulnerability behaviors, while use of glory holes was associated with lower prevalence.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that behaviors associated with higher vulnerability were linked to increased risk of mpox exposure, highlighting the need for targeted public health actions. This study provides novel insights into the psychosocial and behavioral factors influencing health vulnerability among men who have sex with men during mpox outbreaks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of targeted interventions to improve vaccination rates, preventive care, and testing among men who have sex with men during mpox outbreaks, particularly in regions with high prevalence.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study may be limited by potential selection bias, as participants were recruited through online platforms, which might not represent the entire population. The evidence is moderate, as the study is cross-sectional and does not establish causality.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study investigated health vulnerability behaviors among men who have sex with men in Brazil during the mpox outbreak in 2022. The study used an electronic questionnaire to collect data from 1,449 participants, revealing that 13.9% exhibited at least one health vulnerability behavior, such as not being vaccinated against mpox or not undergoing testing. The multivariable analysis identified factors like intimate contact with mpox-positive individuals, non-disclosure of serological status, and disbelief in mpox-related homophobia as independently associated with higher vulnerability. The study highlights the importance of addressing psychosocial barriers to health behaviors in this population. However, the study's reliance on online recruitment may introduce selection bias, limiting the generalizability of the findings. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the study and the lack of longitudinal data.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在分析巴西 猴痘 突发公共卫生事件期间男男性行为者对健康脆弱性行为的遵守情况,解决了解该人群健康脆弱性风险因素的需要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2022 年 9 月至 12 月期间,在虚拟环境中进行了一项横断面分析研究,涉及 1,449 名报告与男性发生性关系的男性。该研究重点关注巴西 猴痘 背景下的健康脆弱性行为。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究使用了 REDCap 平台上托管的电子问卷,通过社交媒体和约会应用程序收集数据。应用具有对数链接函数的广义线性泊松回归模型来分析健康脆弱性行为的 患病率,考虑到结果 患病率 > 10%。
elements_zh.main_results: 在 1,449 名参与者中,13.9%(n=202)报告了至少一种健康脆弱行为,主要原因是未接种 猴痘 疫苗(50.4%)、未采取预防保健措施(30.6%)、未接受检测(26.2%)以及不遵循健康 治疗(9.9%)。多变量模型显示,与 猴痘 患者的亲密接触、不披露血清学状态以及不相信与 猴痘 相关的恐同症与较高的 患病率 脆弱行为独立相关,而使用荣耀洞则与较低的 患病率 相关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,与较高脆弱性相关的行为与 猴痘 暴露风险增加有关,这凸显了采取有针对性的公共卫生行动的必要性。这项研究为影响 猴痘 暴发 期间男男性行为者健康脆弱性的社会心理和行为因素提供了新的见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以为制定有针对性的干预措施提供信息,以提高 猴痘 暴发 期间的男男性行为者的 疫苗接种 率、预防性护理和检测,特别是在 患病率 高的地区。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究可能受到潜在选择偏差的限制,因为参与者是通过在线平台招募的,这可能无法代表整个人群。证据是中等的,因为该研究是横断面的并且没有确定因果关系。

papers.title: Synthesis and Structure−Activity Relationship (SAR) of Hydroxypyridone-3-carboxamides against Orthopoxviruses
papers.abstract: Abstract We have previously identified hydroxypyridone-3-carboxamide 4a as a potent antiviral hit against vaccinia virus (VACV) and monkeypox virus (MPXV), albeit with extremely low solubility. Herein, we have conducted antiviral structure−activity relationship (SAR)-directed and solubility-driven synthesis of a total of 57 analogs. In the primary VACV reporter assay, many analogs demonstrated nanomolar to sub-micromolar antiviral potency without significant cytotoxicity, with analog 4m showing 10-fold improved potency. Plaque assays against VACV and MPXV confirmed the strong antiviral activities. We also discovered that amide N-methylation drastically enhanced solubility via disrupting an intramolecular H-bond. Specifically, we identified an N-methylated analog (4f) with >1000-fold improved solubility while retaining potency (EC50 = 0.69 μM). In addition, compound 4f exhibited dose−response potency against MPXV in the plaque assay and highly favorable ADME properties. Overall, our current work characterizes 4f as a strong antiviral lead and solidifies amide N-methylation as a viable approach toward further lead development.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to develop antiviral compounds with improved potency and solubility against mpox virus and monkeypox virus, building on previous findings that hydroxypyridone-3-carboxamide 4a was a potent antiviral hit against vaccinia virus and monkeypox virus, albeit with low solubility.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the synthesis of 57 analogs of hydroxypyridone-3-carboxamide, with the primary focus on evaluating their antiviral activity against mpox virus and monkeypox virus through in vitro assays.
analysis.methods: The researchers conducted a primary VACV reporter assay to assess antiviral potency and cytotoxicity, and performed plaque assays against VACV and MPXV to confirm antiviral activities. They also evaluated the solubility and ADME properties of compound 4f.
analysis.main_results: Many analogs showed nanomolar to sub-micromolar antiviral potency against VACV and MPXV without significant cytotoxicity, with analog 4m demonstrating 10-fold improved potency. Plaque assays confirmed strong antiviral activities, and compound 4f showed >1000-fold improved solubility while retaining potency (EC50 = 0.69 μM).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as evidence that amide N-methylation significantly enhances solubility without compromising antiviral potency, highlighting compound 4f as a promising lead for further development.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide a foundation for the development of more effective and soluble antiviral agents against mpox virus and monkeypox virus, which could have important implications for treatment and prevention strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro findings and does not include in vivo testing or clinical trials, which reduces the strength of the evidence to moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study focuses on the development of hydroxypyridone-3-carboxamides as antiviral agents against mpox virus and monkeypox virus. Building on prior research that identified 4a as a potent antiviral hit against vaccinia virus and monkeypox virus, the authors synthesized 57 analogs to improve potency and solubility. In vitro assays demonstrated that many analogs showed nanomolar to sub-micromolar antiviral activity against VACV and MPXV, with compound 4f exhibiting >1000-fold improved solubility while maintaining potency (EC50 = 0.69 μM). The authors suggest that amide N-methylation is a viable strategy for enhancing solubility without affecting antiviral efficacy. The findings are significant for future lead development but are limited to in vitro results, which restricts their evidence strength to moderate.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在开发对 猴痘病毒 和猴痘病毒具有改进效力和溶解度的 抗病毒药物 化合物,该研究基于先前的发现,即羟基吡啶酮-3-甲酰胺 4a 是一种有效的 抗病毒药物 对抗痘苗病毒和猴痘病毒的药物,尽管溶解度较低。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及 57 种羟基吡啶酮-3-甲酰胺类似物的合成,主要重点是通过体外测定评估它们对 猴痘病毒 和猴痘病毒的 抗病毒药物 活性。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员进行了主要 VACV 报告基因测定,以评估 抗病毒药物 的效力和细胞毒性,并针对 VACV 和 MPXV 进行了噬菌斑测定,以确认 抗病毒药物 的活性。他们还评估了化合物 4f 的溶解度和 ADME 性质。
elements_zh.main_results: 许多类似物显示出纳摩尔至亚微摩尔 抗病毒药物 对抗 VACV 和 MPXV 的效力,且没有显着的细胞毒性,类似物 4m 的效力提高了 10 倍。噬菌斑测定证实了 抗病毒药物 的强大活性,并且化合物 4f 在保留效​​力的同时显示出超过 1000 倍的溶解度提高 (EC50 = 0.69 μM)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为酰胺 N-甲基化显着提高溶解度而不损害 抗病毒药物 效力的证据,强调化合物 4f 作为进一步开发的有希望的先导化合物。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该结果为开发针对猴痘病毒和猴痘病毒的更有效和可溶的抗病毒药物药物奠定了基础,这可能对治疗和预防策略具有重要意义。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于体外研究结果,不包括体内测试或临床试验,这将证据的强度降至中等。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要:我们之前已经鉴定出羟基吡啶酮-3-甲酰胺 4a 是一种有效的 抗病毒药物 药物,可对抗痘苗病毒 (VACV) 和猴痘病毒 (MPXV),尽管其溶解度极低。在此,我们对总共 57 个类似物进行了 抗病毒药物 构效关系 (SAR) 指导和溶解度驱动的合成。在主要 VACV 报告基因测定中,许多类似物表现出纳摩尔至亚微摩尔 抗病毒药物 效力,而没有显着的细胞毒性,类似物 4m 显示出 10 倍的效力提高。针对 VACV 和 MPXV 的噬菌斑测定证实了 抗病毒药物 的强活性。我们还发现酰胺 N-甲基化通过破坏分子内氢键大大提高了溶解度。具体来说,我们确定了一种 N-甲基化类似物 (4f),其溶解度提高了 1000 倍以上,同时保留了效力 (EC50 = 0.69 μM)。此外,化合物 4f 在空斑测定中表现出针对 MPXV 的剂量反应效力和非常有利的 ADME 特性。总的来说,我们目前的工作将 4f 描述为一种强大的 抗病毒药物 先导化合物,并巩固了酰胺 N-甲基化作为进一步先导化合物开发的可行方法。

papers.title: Probe-Free, Primer-Programmed Amplicon Encoding Enables Nanopore-Based Multiplex Detection With Deep Learning Decoding.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Single‐reaction multiplex nucleic acid testing (NATs) must both co‐amplify multiple targets and distinguish the resulting amplicons within the product mixture. Most conventional assays achieve this distinction using target‐specific reporters or other external encoding elements. Here, we introduce a primer‐programmed multiplexing strategy in which primer design generates target‐associated amplicons with predefined lengths that are read electrically with nanopores. In a proof‐of‐concept implementation, one‐pot recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) generated four amplicons with predefined product lengths from Monkeypox (Mpox), Cowpox, Vaccinia, and human RNase P. The resulting amplicons were analyzed with glass nanopores, and individual translocation events were classified by a deep neural network (DNN) based on a six‐dimensional feature set derived from nanopore recordings. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the challenge of distinguishing multiple targets in single-reaction multiplex nucleic acid testing (NATs), which is critical for accurate detection of pathogens like mpox virus.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study introduced a primer-programmed multiplexing strategy for detecting mpox virus and related entities, using a proof-of-concept implementation with one-pot recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) to generate amplicons from mpox, cowpox, vaccinia, and human RNase P.
analysis.methods: The method involved designing primers to generate target-associated amplicons with predefined lengths, which were then analyzed using glass nanopores and decoded by a deep neural network (DNN) based on a six-dimensional feature set derived from nanopore recordings.
analysis.main_results: Event-level decoding achieved >95% accuracy, >94.7% sensitivity, and >98.3% specificity, with sample-level calls showing >93.3% sensitivity and >93.9% specificity in blinded samples, matching polymerase chain reaction (PCR) results across 9 PCR-benchmarked samples.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The results demonstrate a novel probe-free multiplexing architecture that uses primer-defined amplicon design and deep learning decoding, eliminating the need for target-specific reporter chemistry and enabling all-electrical multiplex nucleic acid testing.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This approach offers new opportunities for rapid, accurate, and cost-effective detection of mpox virus and related pathogens, which could enhance surveillance and diagnostic capabilities for mpox disease.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a proof-of-concept implementation with a small number of benchmarked samples, but the results show high accuracy and specificity, supporting a moderate confidence in the method's potential for broader application.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a novel primer-programmed multiplexing strategy for detecting mpox virus and related pathogens using nanopore-based sequencing and deep learning decoding. The method eliminates the need for probe-specific chemistry, enabling all-electrical detection of multiple targets in a single reaction. In a proof-of-concept implementation, one-pot recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) generated amplicons from mpox, cowpox, vaccinia, and human RNase P, which were analyzed with glass nanopores and classified by a deep neural network (DNN) based on a six-dimensional feature set. Event-level decoding achieved >95% accuracy, >94.7% sensitivity, and >98.3% specificity, with sample-level calls showing >93.3% sensitivity and >93.9% specificity in blinded samples, matching PCR results across 9 benchmarked samples. The findings suggest a promising approach for improving surveillance and diagnostics for mpox virus, though the study is limited to a small set of samples. The evidence supports a moderate confidence in the method's potential for broader application.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决单反应多重核酸检测(NAT)中区分多个目标的挑战,这对于准确检测 猴痘病毒 等病原体至关重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究引入了一种用于检测 猴痘病毒 和相关实体的引物编程多重策略,使用一锅重组酶聚合酶扩增 (RPA) 的概念验证实现来生成来自 猴痘、牛痘、牛痘和人 RNase P 的扩增子。
elements_zh.methods: 该方法涉及设计引物以生成具有预定义长度的目标相关扩增子,然后使用玻璃纳米孔对其进行分析,并通过基于纳米孔记录衍生的六维特征集的深度神经网络(DNN)进行解码。
elements_zh.main_results: 事件级解码实现了 >95% 的准确度、>94.7% 的灵敏度和 >98.3% 的特异性,样本级检测在盲样中显示出 >93.3% 的灵敏度和 >93.9% 的特异性,与 9 个 PCR 基准样本的聚合酶链式反应 (PCR) 结果相匹配。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 结果展示了一种新颖的无探针多重架构,该架构使用引物定义的扩增子设计和深度学习解码,消除了对目标特异性报告化学的需要,并实现了全电多重核酸测试。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这种方法为快速、准确和经济高效地检测 猴痘病毒 和相关病原体提供了新的机会,这可以增强 监测 和 猴痘 疾病的诊断能力。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于使用少量基准样本进行概念验证实施,但结果显示出较高的准确性和特异性,支持对该方法更广泛应用潜力的适度信心。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 单反应多重核酸检测 (NAT) 必须同时扩增多个靶标并区分产物混合物中产生的扩增子。大多数传统测定使用目标特异性报告基因或其他外部编码元件来实现这种区别。在这里,我们引入了一种引物编程的多重策略,其中引物设计生成具有预定义长度的目标相关扩增子,这些扩增子可以通过纳米孔进行电读取。在概念验证实施中,一锅重组酶聚合酶扩增 (RPA) 生成了来自猴痘 (猴痘)、牛痘、牛痘和人 RNase P 的四个具有预定义产物长度的扩增子。使用玻璃纳米孔分析所得扩增子,并通过基于纳米孔记录衍生的六维特征集的深度神经网络 (DNN) 对各个易位事件进行分类。事件级解码实现了 >95% 的准确度、>94.7% 的灵敏度和 >98.3% 的特异性,分类事件的聚合在盲样样本中产生了 >93.3% 的灵敏度和 >93.9% 的特异性的样本级判别,定性判别与 9 个 PCR 基准样本中的聚合酶链式反应 (PCR) 结果相匹配。这些结果展示了一种无探针多重架构,其中目标身份通过引物定义的扩增子设计进行编程,并使用 DNN 从生成的多维纳米孔响应中进行解码,消除了对目标特异性报告化学的需要,并为基于未修饰的扩增产物的全电多重核酸测试开辟了新的机会。

papers.title: Reassessing the diversity and distribution of African rope squirrels ( Funisciurus Trouessart, 1880) in the Congo Basin
papers.abstract: Abstract The taxonomy, distribution, and ecology of sub-Saharan squirrels are poorly documented. This study focuses on the diversity and distribution of rope squirrels (Funisciurus Trouessart, 1880) in the Congo Basin. We compiled the most comprehensive genetic (n = 397 sequences) and morphometric (n = 219 measured skulls) dataset to date, covering much of their geographical and taxonomic range. Analysis of mitochondrial markers recovered 10 MOTUs (Molecular Operational Taxonomic Unit), nuclear markers 2 MOTUs, and morphometrics 5 Operational Taxonomic Units. Integrating this evidence suggests at least six species-level lineages in our dataset: four allopatric taxa related to F. anerythrus; four genetically different taxa (of which two are sympatric species) that resemble F. bayonii; one taxon corresponding to F. pyrropus akka de Winton, 1895; one morphologically distinct taxon that resembles F. congicus; and one unidentified taxon. Their distributional ranges reveal that the Congo and Kasaï Rivers act as major biogeographical barriers, suggesting that they originated by allopatric speciation. Our findings provide a baseline for studying the effects of habitat loss on rope squirrel populations in the Congo Basin and inform research into their role as reservoirs of zoonotic pathogens, including mpox virus.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在重新评估刚果盆地非洲绳松鼠的多样性和分布,因为它们的分类、分布和生态学记录很少。该研究还强调需要了解它们作为人畜共患病原体(包括 猴痘病毒)的潜在 储存宿主 的作用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究编制了迄今为止最全面的遗传(n = 397 个序列)和形态测量(n = 219 个测量头骨)数据集,涵盖了非洲绳松鼠的大部分地理和分类范围。该分析重点关注刚果盆地,目的是确定物种层面的谱系和生物地理模式。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员分析了线粒体标记、核标记和形态测量数据,以确定分子操作分类单位(MOTU)。他们综合这些发现来确定松鼠的分布范围和物种形成模式。
elements_zh.main_results: 线粒体标记分析恢复了 10 个 MOTU,核标记恢复了 2 个 MOTU,形态测量恢复了 5 个操作分类单位。该研究鉴定出至少六种物种级谱系,包括与 F. anerythrus 相关的 4 个异域类群、与 F. bayonii 类似的 4 个遗传上不同的类群、与 1895 年 F. Pyropus akka de Winton 相对应的一种分类群、与 F. congicus 类似的形态上不同的分类群以及一种未识别的分类群。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 遗传和形态测量数据的整合表明刚果河和开赛河是主要的生物地理屏​​障,表明该物种起源于异域物种形成。这一发现为了解该地区绳松鼠的进化历史和分布提供了新的见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为研究栖息地丧失对绳松鼠种群的影响提供了基线,并为研究它们作为人畜共患病原体(包括 猴痘病毒)的 储存宿主 的作用提供了信息。这对于了解刚果盆地 猴痘 的生态和潜在 猴痘 动态具有重要意义。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于仅抽象的证据基础,这可能会限制分析的深度。然而,综合数据集和多个标记的整合为关于绳松鼠多样性和分布的结论提供了中等程度的可信度。

papers.full_text: ABSTRACTSingle‐reaction multiplex nucleic acid testing (NATs) must both co‐amplify multiple targets and distinguish the resulting amplicons within the product mixture. Most conventional assays achieve this distinction using target‐specific reporters or other external encoding elements. Here, we introduce a primer‐programmed multiplexing strategy in which primer design generates target‐associated amplicons with predefined lengths that are read electrically with nanopores. In a proof‐of‐concept implementation, one‐pot recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) generated four amplicons with predefined product lengths from Monkeypox (Mpox), Cowpox, Vaccinia, and human RNase P. The resulting amplicons were analyzed with glass nanopores, and individual translocation events were classified by a deep neural network (DNN) based on a six‐dimensional feature set derived from nanopore recordings. Event‐level decoding achieved >95% accuracy, >94.7% sensitivity, and >98.3% specificity, and aggregation of classified events yielded sample‐level calls with >93.3% sensitivity and >93.9% specificity in blinded samples, with qualitative calls matching polymerase chain reaction (PCR) results across the 9 PCR‐benchmarked samples. These results demonstrate a probe‐free multiplexing architecture in which target identity is programmed through primer‐defined amplicon design and decoded from the resulting multidimensional nanopore response using a DNN, eliminating the need for target‐specific reporter chemistry and opening new opportunities for all‐electrical multiplex nucleic acid testing based on unmodified amplification products.Keywords: deep learning, molecular diagnostics, multiplex nucleic acid testing, primer‐programmed amplicon encoding, recombinase polymerase amplification, solid‐state nanopore sensing Primer‐programmed amplicon encoding enables reporter‐probe‐free multiplex nucleic acid identification using glass nanopore sensing and deep neural network decoding. 4.Methods and Experimental Section4.1.Materials and ChemicalsQuantitative synthetic Mpox DNA (VR‐3270SD, 100 μL, 2.8 × 105 copies μL−1) and Cowpox DNA (VR‐302) were purchased from ATCC. Human RNase P DNA (Hs RPP30 Positive Control, 10006626) and gBlocks gene fragments for Vaccinia were obtained from Integrated DNA Technologies (IDT). Key materials, 100 bp DNA Ladder (#N0467S), Gel Loading Dye, Purple (6X) (#B7025), and nuclease‐free water (B1500), were purchased from New England Biolabs Inc. (NEB). Additional reagents, such as TaqMan Fast Virus 1‐Step Multiplex Master Mix (#5555532) and Tris‐EDTA buffer, were acquired from Thermo Fisher and Sigma‐Aldrich. Biotium GelRed Nucleic Acid Gel Stain, 10 000× (#NC9594719), was purchased from Fisher Scientific. RPA reaction kits and enzymes (#TALQBAS01) were provided by TwistDx Ltd (Cambridge, UK). Experimental components, including quartz capillaries (0.5 mm inner diameter and 1 mm outer diameter; Sutter Instrument, USA), silver wire (0.008 inches, 25 feet), and accessories such as pipette holders (#663040), seals (#647110), and pin connectors (#647110), were sourced from A‐M Systems. A microinjector equipped with 34‐gauge needles was also purchased from World Precision Instruments.4.2.RPA AssayDesign. Synthetic DNA fragments were designed from the Mpox F3L region (nt 46,344–46,453; ON563414.3), the Cowpox F3L region (nt 63,463–63,703; based on the ATCC reference sequence and similar to Cowpox Brighton, AF482758), and the Vaccinia A56R region (nt 162,298–162,746; NC_006998.1), together with the RNase P target (nt 100–409). Primers were designed to match these regions (Table S1), and sequence specificity was verified by BLAST. Primer quality was assessed using the TwistDx RPA primer‐design guidelines and the PrimedRPA open‐source Python code [53]. Candidate primers were screened for primer length, GC content, repeat regions, and sequence specificity, and potential primer interactions, including hairpin formation, self‐dimerization, and hetero‐dimerization, were evaluated to minimize predicted primer‐primer interactions. Singleplex Reaction. Each RPA reaction (Table S2) was prepared in a 25 μL total volume containing 1.25 μL each of forward and reverse primers (500 nM), 12.50 μL of 2× RPA reaction buffer (1X), 2.50 μL of 10× Basic E‐mix (1X), 2.00 μL of dNTP mix (800–2000 μM), 1.25 μL of 20× Core Reaction Mix (1X), 2.00 μL of nuclease‐free water, and 1.00 μL of the appropriate target template (Mpox, Cowpox, human RNase P, or Vaccinia; 2 × 105 copies μL−1). 1.25 μL Magnesium acetate (Mg(AcO)2) was added last, at 14 mM, to prevent premature initiation of the reaction, yielding a 23.75 μL master mixture before reaction initiation. Reactions were incubated at 39°C for 20 min. Multiplex Reaction. Multiplex RPA reactions were prepared in a 25 μL total volume (23.75 μL master mixture plus 1.25 μL Mg(AcO)2) and were incubated at 39°C for 20 min. In duplex, triplex, and four‐plex formats, each primer was maintained at an adjustable final concentration of 400–500 nM to balance amplification across targets. The same 2× RPA buffer and 10× Basic E‐mix used in singleplex reactions were used for multiplex assays. The dNTP mix was used at a final concentration of 1000–2400 μM, depending on the multiplex level. The 20× Core Reaction Mix was adjusted 1.0–1.6× to support higher multiplex complexity. Template inputs were 105 copies μL−1 stocks for duplex, triplex, and four‐plex reactions to maintain the total template volume. Mg(AcO)2 was added as the final step to initiate the reaction. Detailed formulations are provided in Tables S3–S5. Gel analysis of RPA amplicons. After RPA, the amplicons were resolved by 3% agarose gel electrophoresis at 6 V/cm using GelRed stain. The bands of interest were then analyzed using the BIO‐RAD GelDoc Go Imaging System with a 20‐s exposure.4.3.PCR AssayPCR reactions (Tables S6–S9) were prepared in a 20 μL total volume using TaqMan Fast Virus 1‐Step (Multiplex) Master Mix at 1× final concentration. Primer concentrations were maintained at 600 nM final for singleplex reactions and adjusted to final concentrations of 400–600 nM final per primer for duplex, triplex, and four‐plex formats to balance amplification across targets. Target templates were prepared at a concentration of 105 copies μL−1. Amplicons were resolved on a 3% agarose gel run at 6 V/cm with GelRed staining, and bands were imaged using a BIO‐RAD GelDoc Go Imaging System with a 20‐s exposure.4.4.Nanopore Fabrication and MeasurementQuartz capillaries were cleaned in a Piranha solution (H2SO4:H2O2 = 3:1) at 85°C for 30 min, then rinsed with deionized water and dried in a vacuum oven at 120°C for 20 min. Nanopores were fabricated using a laser pipette puller (P‐2000, Sutter Instruments, USA) under a single‐line protocol (heat 650, filament 4, velocity 60, delay 145, pull 160–215) and two‐line protocol (Line 1: “heat 750, filament 5, velocity 50, delay 140, and pull 50” and Line 2: “heat 715, filament 4, velocity 30, delay 145, and pull 215–245” signal‐to‐noise ratio) [54, 55, 56]. The finished pores were filled with either 1 M KCl, 2 M LiCl, or 4 M LiCl in Tris‐EDTA buffer (pH 8.0), and electrolyte solutions were filtered through a 0.2 μm syringe filter (WHA67802502, Whatman) before use [57]. Amplification products were passed through the same 0.2 μm filter and diluted 20‐fold prior to measurement, so that the recorded signals originated predominantly from the target amplicons. A constant voltage was applied using a NI‐6363 DAQ card (National Instruments, USA), and the ionic current was amplified with an Axopatch 200B amplifier (Molecular Devices, USA) [54, 55]. Data were sampled at 100 kHz, low‐pass filtered at 10 kHz in LabVIEW, and recorded inside a custom Faraday cage using Ag/AgCl electrodes in the cis and trans chambers, with the cis side grounded.4.5.Data Collection and AnalysisNanopore data for DNN training were collected from 66 samples measured using 21 nanopores in Figure S14. The diameters of these model‐training pores ranged from 4.70 to 11.44 nm, confirming that the training data spanned a broad pore‐size distribution (Figure S15F). Approximately 100–300 translocation events were acquired per sample, corresponding to an expected Poisson counting uncertainty of ∼10%–5.8%, respectively [44]. For each event, ΔI, Δt, IB, and IRMS were extracted within a 1000 ms window centered on the event, comprising 500 ms before and 500 ms after the event. IB and IRMS were treated as event‐specific local descriptors rather than fixed global values for an entire pore or recording. ΔI was calculated relative to the event‐specific local baseline, reducing the influence of absolute current offsets between pores and slow baseline drift within a recording. These acquisition and quality‐control criteria minimized the influence of temporal drift on ΔI and Δt during individual measurements. For feature‐space visualization, t‐SNE was applied to standardized six‐feature input vectors and to the penultimate‐layer activations extracted from the trained DNN. To assess the pore‐size dependence of DNN performance within the selected broad diameter window, overall event‐level accuracy was calculated separately for each nanopore diameter as the proportion of events correctly assigned to A1‐A4 or NT. Post‐processing and peak extractions were performed using custom Python 3.13.3 scripts, keeping the signal‐to‐noise ratio (SNR) >3. Peaks were detected using a threshold of μ′ + 3σ′, where μ′ and σ′ denote the mean and standard deviation of the baseline current. A held‐out validation dataset consisting of 23 samples measured on independent nanopores was used for intermediate model evaluation (Figure S16). A separate 62‐sample blinded cohort was subsequently evaluated using sample preparations and physical nanopores that were not represented in the 66‐sample development dataset. This cohort was not used for feature selection, hyperparameter optimization, or model weight updating and therefore served as an independent unseen‐sample and unseen‐pore evaluation of the fixed classifier. For sample‐level calling, NTC event rates were calculated by dividing the number of detected events by the corresponding acquisition duration for each replicate. Approximate normality was evaluated using the Shapiro‐Wilk test and Q‐Q analysis. The sample‐level decision threshold was defined as μ + 3σ of the NTC event‐rate distribution and was applied only after DNN event classification. Sample‐level sensitivity and specificity are reported with two‐sided 95% exact binomial CI calculated using the Clopper–Pearson method. 4.1.Materials and ChemicalsQuantitative synthetic Mpox DNA (VR‐3270SD, 100 μL, 2.8 × 105 copies μL−1) and Cowpox DNA (VR‐302) were purchased from ATCC. Human RNase P DNA (Hs RPP30 Positive Control, 10006626) and gBlocks gene fragments for Vaccinia were obtained from Integrated DNA Technologies (IDT). Key materials, 100 bp DNA Ladder (#N0467S), Gel Loading Dye, Purple (6X) (#B7025), and nuclease‐free water (B1500), were purchased from New England Biolabs Inc. (NEB). Additional reagents, such as TaqMan Fast Virus 1‐Step Multiplex Master Mix (#5555532) and Tris‐EDTA buffer, were acquired from Thermo Fisher and Sigma‐Aldrich. Biotium GelRed Nucleic Acid Gel Stain, 10 000× (#NC9594719), was purchased from Fisher Scientific. RPA reaction kits and enzymes (#TALQBAS01) were provided by TwistDx Ltd (Cambridge, UK). Experimental components, including quartz capillaries (0.5 mm inner diameter and 1 mm outer diameter; Sutter Instrument, USA), silver wire (0.008 inches, 25 feet), and accessories such as pipette holders (#663040), seals (#647110), and pin connectors (#647110), were sourced from A‐M Systems. A microinjector equipped with 34‐gauge needles was also purchased from World Precision Instruments. In this framework, probe‐free multiplexing is achieved by designing RPA primer sets that produce amplicons with distinct lengths, such that target identity is encoded directly in the amplification products. Figure 1A outlines the overall workflow. A sample containing four representative targets (M, C, R, and V) is amplified in a single RPA reaction to generate length‐defined amplicons. (A) Schematic of the multiplex amplification and nanopore sensing workflow. Four targets (M, C, R, and V) are amplified in a single reaction to generate amplicons with distinct lengths (A1, A2, A3, and A4). The resulting amplicons translocate through a glass nanopore and generate ionic current signals recorded as I–t traces. Six quantitative features are extracted from each event: baseline current, RMS current, blockade amplitude, dwell time, time since the previous event, and nanopore diameter. (B) Event caller: A DNN model is trained on these six features to assign individual events to one of five classes: A1, A2, A3, A4, or NT. Feature vectors propagate through multiple nonlinear hidden layers to produce predicted classes. (C) Target caller: Event classifications from blinded samples are aggregated to calculate target‐specific event rates over the acquisition period. A target is called positive when the event rate exceeds a statistical threshold defined as μ + 3σ of the event‐rate distribution measured across NTC replicates.To prepare raw nanopore recordings for DNN‐based decoding, each detected translocation event was converted into a quantitative feature vector. Six event‐level features were extracted: baseline current (IB), root‐mean‐square (RMS) current (IRMS), blockade amplitude (ΔI), dwell time (Δt), time since the previous event (t), and nanopore diameter (D). IB and IRMS describe the local baseline and noise environment, whereas ΔI and Δt describe the individual current‐blockade event; t captures the temporal spacing between consecutive events, and D accounts for pore‐dependent signal scaling. Representative feature extraction and event‐level values are shown in Figure S1. Primer design defines target‐associated amplicons with distinct product lengths, while the six extracted features characterize their multidimensional nanopore responses. Because the four amplicons also differ in sequence composition, the present study does not isolate sequence‐independent length discrimination. The DNN therefore decodes the composite electrical response of the primer‐programmed amplicons, with local baseline, noise, temporal spacing, and pore size providing contextual information needed to accommodate temporal and sensor‐to‐sensor variability.We asked whether primer‐programmed RPA products could be reliably distinguished using conventional single‐parameter or two‐parameter nanopore descriptors alone. We examined blockade amplitude‐dwell time (ΔI‐Δt) distributions and event charge deficit (ECD) values for the four singleplex target classes. As shown in Figure S2, the ΔI–Δt distributions for M, C, R, and V showed substantial overlap. Adjacent‐target ECD comparisons using two‐sided Welch's t‐tests yielded p = 0.318 (M vs. C), p = 6.5 × 10−6 (C vs. R), and p = 0.056 (R vs. V), with two of the three comparisons not statistically significant. These results indicate that conventional low‐dimensional nanopore descriptors are insufficient for robust multiplex decoding.We therefore asked whether combining multiple event‐level and pore‐related features could improve discrimination. To capture multidimensional and potentially nonlinear relationships among these features, we trained a DNN to classify individual nanopore events using the six features. The model assigns each event to one of five event classes: four target‐associated amplicon classes (A1‐A4) or a non‐target (NT) class (Figure 1B). The NT class was included to represent events that do not match the four target‐associated amplicon classes, including background species, nonspecific products, and RPA‐associated artifacts. This design allowed the classifier to use multiple signal descriptors simultaneously. To visualize whether the six‐feature representation contained class‐associated information beyond conventional nanopore descriptors, we analyzed representative 3‐plex and 4‐plex datasets using t‐distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t‐SNE). As shown in Figure S3, t‐SNE projections of the standardized raw six‐feature input vectors showed partial class‐associated structure, but the target classes remained closely positioned and partially overlapping, indicating that the raw feature space was not fully separable. In contrast, t‐SNE projections of the penultimate‐layer DNN representation showed clearer class organization after nonlinear transformation by the trained network. (B) Event caller: A DNN model is trained on these six features to assign individual events to one of five classes: A1, A2, A3, A4, or NT. Feature vectors propagate through multiple nonlinear hidden layers to produce predicted classes. (C) Target caller: Event classifications from blinded samples are aggregated to calculate target‐specific event rates over the acquisition period. A target is called positive when the event rate exceeds a statistical threshold defined as μ + 3σ of the event‐rate distribution measured across NTC replicates.To prepare raw nanopore recordings for DNN‐based decoding, each detected translocation event was converted into a quantitative feature vector. Six event‐level features were extracted: baseline current (IB), root‐mean‐square (RMS) current (IRMS), blockade amplitude (ΔI), dwell time (Δt), time since the previous event (t), and nanopore diameter (D). IB and IRMS describe the local baseline and noise environment, whereas ΔI and Δt describe the individual current‐blockade event; t captures the temporal spacing between consecutive events, and D accounts for pore‐dependent signal scaling. Representative feature extraction and event‐level values are shown in Figure S1. Primer design defines target‐associated amplicons with distinct product lengths, while the six extracted features characterize their multidimensional nanopore responses. Because the four amplicons also differ in sequence composition, the present study does not isolate sequence‐independent length discrimination. The DNN therefore decodes the composite electrical response of the primer‐programmed amplicons, with local baseline, noise, temporal spacing, and pore size providing contextual information needed to accommodate temporal and sensor‐to‐sensor variability.We asked whether primer‐programmed RPA products could be reliably distinguished using conventional single‐parameter or two‐parameter nanopore descriptors alone. As shown in Figure S2, the ΔI–Δt distributions for M, C, R, and V showed substantial overlap. Adjacent‐target ECD comparisons using two‐sided Welch's t‐tests yielded p = 0.318 (M vs. C), p = 6.5 × 10−6 (C vs. R), and p = 0.056 (R vs. V), with two of the three comparisons not statistically significant. The model assigns each event to one of five event classes: four target‐associated amplicon classes (A1‐A4) or a non‐target (NT) class (Figure 1B). The NT class was included to represent events that do not match the four target‐associated amplicon classes, including background species, nonspecific products, and RPA‐associated artifacts. This design allowed the classifier to use multiple signal descriptors simultaneously. In contrast, t‐SNE projections of the penultimate‐layer DNN representation showed clearer class organization after nonlinear transformation by the trained network. For each sample, the total measurement time T was defined as the sum of the inter‐event intervals t 1 to t N (Figure 1C), and target‐specific event rates were calculated over the corresponding acquisition period. A target was called positive when its DNN‐assigned event rate exceeded the pre‐established μ + 3σ = 0.14 Hz NTC threshold, where μ = 0.066 Hz and σ = 0.024 Hz. The NTC background distribution was characterized using 11 independent measurements, and the event‐rate distribution showed no significant departure from normality by the Shapiro‐Wilk test (p = 0.21) (Figure S4A–D). Importantly, the DNN was fully trained and fixed before threshold estimation. The μ + 3σ criterion was therefore applied only as a downstream sample‐level decision boundary and did not participate in event‐level model training or target assignment. Under these conditions, target‐associated amplicons typically produced event rates above this threshold, whereas background species and inherent RPA artifacts produced sparse, low‐frequency events that remained below threshold and were often characterized by longer dwell times (Figure S5A).
